 Objective of Event : The objective of a project presentation competition is to showcase participants 
ability to effectively communicate and articulate their project’s purpose, methodology and outcomes . 
It fosters the development of essential skills such as public speaking, critical thinking and presentation 
design. Participants aim to engage the audience, convey the significance of their project and 
demonstrate its innovative aspects. This competitive platform encourages creativity, professionalism 
and the ability to distill complex information into a compelling and concise presentation. Overall, the 
competition promotes excellence in communication and highlights the merits of each project within a 
competitive framework . 
 Outcome of the Event  : The project presentation competition yielded diverse outcomes as 
participants showcased innovative ideas and solutions. Judges evaluated based on clarity, creativity, 
and feasibility. Winners demonstrated exceptional communication skills, addressing queries 
effectively. Their projects spanned various fields, from technology to social impact, reflecting the 
competition's interdisciplinary nature. The event fostered knowledge exchange, inspiring participants

Abhivyakti 
A National Level Paper Presentation Event 
 21st and 22nd February, 2026  
The paper presentation event has been successfully carried out in the following three different venues 
of our institute with broad objectives.  
1) KIT IRF conference hall  
2) IDEA Lab Seminar Hall  
3) E-content Seminar Hall  
The primary objective of the said event was to provide a platform for UG, PG, Ph.D. students to engage 
in academic, professional, and personal development through presentations their own research work 
as well as sharing their own research ideas.  
Apart from this, the major objectives of the event are:  
 To provide a prestigious national forum for students, researchers, and academicians to 
showcase innovative ideas, research findings, and technical advancements.  
 To cultivate a robust research culture and scientific temperament by fostering analytical 
thinking, creative problem-solving, and intellectual curiosity.  
 To refine the presentation and communication skills of participants through structured, 
professional technical paper presentations.  
 To facilitate knowledge exchange and academic networking among participants from diverse 
institutions across the country.  
 To inspire students to pursue higher education and advanced research by exposing them to 
emerging technologies and diverse research domains.  
 To bridge the gap between academic theory and practical application by addressing real-world 
challenges with innovative solutions. 
  
Outcome of the Event : In alignment with the event's objectives, we received an overwhelming 
response from across India. A total of 110 student groups registered for the paper presentations, 
contributing 110 research papers across both Circuit and Non-Circuit domains. Throughout the event, 
our Peer Review Committee meticulously evaluated each paper based on the quality of the research 
and the impact of the presentation.  
Registration Fee : Rs. 200/- per participants.  
Details of Prize : 1st Prize-Rs. 15000/-  
1st Runner up Prize- Rs. 10000/-  
2nd Runner up Prize- Rs. 10000/-  
No. of Registrations: Total 110 student groups have been registered.  
Within the state: 105 student groups  
Out of state: 05 student groups

4 Theme of Event and description: "Master Bidder 2026" (The Art of Bridge Construction with 
Limited Budgets) Master Bidder 2026 challenges the traditional technical approach by blending civil 
engineering principles with economic strategy and project management. The event simulates a real-
world construction environment where participants must strategically procure materials and execute a 
building task. Divided into three distinct rounds, the competition tests not only structural knowledge 
but also financial acumen and negotiation skills, mirroring the challenges faced by real-world 
contractors and project managers.  
5 Objective of Event:  
• Enhance understanding of material properties and construction costs.  
• Develop strategic thinking through budget allocation and resource management.  
• Foster teamwork and time management skills are under pressure.  
• Bridge the gap between academic knowledge and practical industry applications, specifically in 
project bidding and execution.  
6 Outcome of the Event :  
• A deeper understanding of how financial constraints impact design and construction choices.  
• Improved problem-solving abilities, particularly in optimizing structures with limited resources.  
Registration Fee : ₹300 per group (Maximum of 4 participants per group.)

Name of Event : IDEA-FORGED 2026

3 Name of Department : Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering  
4 Theme of Event and description :  
• Theme : “Ignite. Forge. Innovate.”  
• Description : Idea-Forged is a national-level technical innovation competition that challenges 
participants to conceptualize and develop impactful engineering solutions.  
Organized by the Department of Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering, the event provides a 
platform for students to transform creative ideas into practical implementations.  
The competition unfolds in two elimination rounds:  
Round 1 – Ignite the Idea:  
Teams present a novel and technically sound idea addressing a real-world problem.  
Round 2 – Forge the Solution:  
Shortlisted teams further develop their concept into a detailed solution, prototype, or implementation 
model.  
The event encourages interdisciplinary innovation across domains such as IoT, Robotics, 
Mechatronics, Electronics, Embedded Systems, Hardware, Software, and Tech-driven Business 
solutions.  
Objective of Event :  
Idea-Forged aims to inspire students to transform innovative ideas into practical engineering solutions. 
The event encourages creative problem-solving, technical excellence, and teamwork while addressing 
real-world challenges. It seeks to bridge the gap between conceptual thinking and real-time 
implementation, fostering a spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship.  
Outcome of the Event :  
Idea-Forged turned out to be a highly engaging and successful event, with 113 teams actively 
participating and presenting a wide range of innovative ideas. The enthusiasm and creativity displayed 
by the students were truly commendable. The competition not only encouraged technical thinking but 
also helped participants improve their presentation skills, teamwork, and practical approach toward 
problem-solving. Overall, the event created an inspiring environment that motivated students to think 
beyond the classroom and work towards real-world solutions.

 Theme of Event: Stranger Things  
Objective of Event: The objective of Stranger Code: Escape the Upside Down is to provide 
students with a competitive platform to test and enhance their problem-solving abilities, logical 
thinking, and programming skills. The event focuses on improving participants’ aptitude, puzzle-
solving capabilities, and coding proficiency, which are essential for technical interviews and 
placement preparation. Through multiple elimination rounds, the competition encourages students to 
develop analytical thinking, time management, and algorithmic problem-solving skills while 
promoting excellence in technical knowledge and innovation.

abilities, and analytical thinking. Students gained hands-on experience solving real programming 
problems under time constraints, which is beneficial for technical interviews and competitive 
programming. Also created an engaging learning environment that promoted teamwork, creativity, 
and continuous learning while connecting students from various institutions interested in technology 
and programming.  
Registration Fee: Rs. 100/-  
Details of Event:  
Stranger Code: Escape the Upside Down was a coding competition organized by the Department 
of Computer Science and Engineering under Pioneer 2026. The event consisted of three 
elimination rounds: Aptitude, Puzzle with Pseudocode, and Coding. Participants solved 40 aptitude 
questions, 40 puzzle/pseudocode questions, and finally 6 coding problems using C, C++, Java, or 
Python. The event aimed to test students’ logical thinking, problem-solving skills, and 
programming abilities

Information about club – 
E-Cell KITCoEK, also known as The Entrepreneurship Cell of KIT’s College of Engineering, 
Kolhapur, is a student-driven initiative dedicated to promoting entrepreneurship, innovation, and 
leadership among students under the tagline “Think. Innovate. Implement.” The cell provides aspiring 
entrepreneurs with a platform to transform creative ideas into successful ventures by offering 
mentorship, networking opportunities, resources, and practical exposure to the startup ecosystem. 
E-Cell KITCoEK actively contributes to building an entrepreneurial culture within the campus by 
organizing workshops, startup competitions, guest lectures, and interactive sessions with industry 
professionals and successful entrepreneurs. One of its major initiatives is the E-Summit, the flagship 
entrepreneurship event of the college, which brings together startup enthusiasts, investors, innovators, 
and business leaders from across the country. The summit features activities such as Business Expo, 
finance and stock market workshops, pitching competitions, and speaker sessions with renowned 
entrepreneurs, including personalities featured on shows like Shark Tank India. Along with events like 
Illuminate, Pitching Deck, and the ECR Program, E-Cell KITCoEK continuously inspires students to 
develop innovative thinking and practical business skills.

literacy program organized to help students develop innovative thinking, business 
understanding, and financial awareness. The event featured expert sessions by dignitaries 
including Sunil Bharadwaj Sir, Nilesh Jain, and Chairperson Reva Patil.  
The program covered important topics such as investment planning, stock markets, mutual 
funds, SIPs, entrepreneurship fundamentals, and startup financial concepts. Mr. Nilesh 
Jain explained key financial ideas like assets, Gold ETFs, government bonds, and risk 
management in investments.

elevator pitching, SWOT analysis, customer segmentation, and Business Model Canvas

BMC exercises encouraged practical learning, teamwork, and analytical thinking.

2025 proved to be an engaging and educational experience that motivated participants to 
think creatively and pursue entrepreneurial opportunities.

3. E-Heist 
E-Heist was a two-day academic and experiential event conducted on 12th and 13th 
October with the objective of enhancing students’ analytical reasoning, creativity, 
teamwork, and strategic thinking through an engaging heist-themed format. The event 
created an immersive learning environment that combined intellectual challenges with 
practical skill development. It was inaugurated in the presence of esteemed dignitaries 
including Sachin Shinde Sir, Jitendra Bhatt Sir, and Dr. Saee Thakur Ma’am.

11 
 
The first day began with a formal inauguration ceremony followed by a session on trading 
and financial concepts. Students gained valuable insights into market behavior, investment 
decisions, and trading strategies, helping them improve their financial awareness and 
understanding of investment fundamentals.  
To align with the event’s theme, participants dressed as thieves and presented a themed 
entry, which added excitement and audience engagement. Students were then divided into 
groups for competitive activities. One group participated in the Heist Activity, which 
included puzzles, riddles, and problem-solving tasks that tested logical reasoning, 
teamwork, time management, and decision-making abilities. The second group 
participated in the Advertisement Activity, where students created and presented 
innovative advertisements based on assigned themes.  
The second day featured the U25 Summit, which included performances, interactive 
sessions, and engaging discussions with invited guests. Ms. Mrunal Divekar shared 
inspiring insights about her professional journey, challenges, and determination, 
motivating students to pursue their goals with confidence and perseverance. Rapid 
interactive rounds were also conducted to encourage quick thinking and adaptability 
among participants.  
Overall, E-Heist was successfully conducted and proved to be an educational as well as 
entertaining experience. The event helped students develop important skills such as 
analytical thinking, communication, creativity, collaboration, and decision-making while 
encouraging active participation and practical learning.

Summary of School Visit: 
On August 19, 2025, an outreach program at New English School in Khupire reached 140 students across 
the 8th, 9th, and 10th grades to focus on skill development, career planning, and social responsibility. The 
initiative featured an in -depth Career Guidance session covering Science, Diploma, Arts, Commerce, 
Defense and Police sectors. Concurrently, Digital Literacy workshops taught students to navigate social 
media responsibly, identify online scams, manage screen time, and utilize online resources for learning. 
The program also engaged students through interactive games, including "Gra b n Go" for patience and 
"Tagline Takkar" for critical thinking, alongside a social awareness play titled "Importance of Choices" that 
addressed bullying, gaming addiction, and daily decision-making.

Summary of INVICTA: 
On October 12 and 13, 2025, the flagship two-day workshop series INVICTA provided free, project-based 
technical and creative training to 279 participants across four specialized tracks. The Full -Stack Web 
Development track guided 75 participants through frontend and backend technologies to build responsive, 
scalable applications. The 3D Design and Modeling track trained 70 participants in Blender fundamentals, 
including texturing, rendering, and animation. The Photography and Post -Processing track instructed 62 
participants on manual camera modes, composition, and advanced editing software. Concurrently, the IoT 
and Microcontrollers track taught 72 participants automation and integration using the ESP8266 through 
guided hardware projects. Each track recognized a top performer at its conclusion.

Summary of VERBAFEST: 
On February 9, 2026, the placement -oriented event VERBAFEST drew 180 participants to simulate 
recruitment processes across three competitive tracks. The first track evaluated candidates through a 
digitized Aptitude Test, a Gamified Assessment, and an Engli sh proficiency Versant Test, utilizing Team 
Maverick’s secured online platform to ensure integrity. The Group Discussion track evaluated 
communication through general, abstract, and situational rounds, concluding with the Debate track tested 
rapid point ge neration and critical thinking by slashing preparation time and introducing a mid -debate 
twist that forced teams to instantly swap opposing viewpoints. Top performers were crowned as winners

activity designed to boost team synchronization and rapid decision -making. Transitioning to academic 
skills, a specialized session on Higher Studi es compared domestic M.Tech routes with international MS 
degrees while outlining the fundamentals and portfolio value of drafting research papers. Team strategy

started with a silent outdoor coordination activity that used non-verbal tasks, like arranging sequences by 
birthdates without speaking, to emphasize body language and intuitive teamwork. A technical productivity 
session followed, demonstrating how to strategically leverage modern AI tools to improve everyday 
efficiency and academic work. Group problem-solving and quick thinking were practiced under pressure

the 8th, 9th, and 10th grades to focus on skill development, career planning, and social responsibility. The

Information about club – The Student Developers Club serves as an excellent platform for students 
to enhance their technical knowledge, creativity, leadership qualities, and teamwork skills beyond 
the classroom environment. Through workshops, seminars, coding activities, technical competitions, 
and interactive sessions, the club encourages students to explore emerging technologies and develop 
practical problem-solving abilities. It helps bridge the gap between academic learning and industry 
expectations by providing opportunities for hands-on experience, peer learning, and interaction with

Summary of Each Activity 
1) Effective Strategies for the Placement Preparation 
The Student Developers Club at KIT’s College of Engineering, Kolhapur in association with ACADS, 
Department of CSE (AIML and DS) successfully conducted a one-day workshop on “Effective Strategies 
for Placement Preparation” on Saturday, 19/07/2025 from 11:15 am to 5:00 pm. 
Nearly than 200 students benefitted from this workshop. The session provided valuable insights into 
placement preparation strategies, aptitude training, resume building, interview techniques, and 
communication skills required for campus recruitment drives. Students actively participated in 
various interactive activities and gained practical guidance for improving their placement readiness. 
The enthusiasm and involvement of students throughout the session were truly remarkable. 
A big thanks to Mr. Atharva Patil, Algorizz Technologies Private Limited, Ms. Shreya Chavan, Placed 
in Cogitate Technology Solutions , for sharing their valuable industry experience and expert 
guidance. We also appreciate all the students for their active participation and keen interest in 
enhancing their professional skills. 
The participants of this workshop benefitted with practical knowledge and strategies related to 
placement preparation, aptitude problem-solving, resume enhancement, and interview handling 
techniques. Following are the outcomes of this workshop: 
1. Understanding effective strategies for campus placement preparation and planning a 
structured roadmap for achieving placement goals. 
2. Learning techniques to improve aptitude, logical reasoning, and problem-solving skills 
required for placement tests. 
3. Developing professional resumes, improving communication skills, and gaining confidence 
for technical as well as HR interviews. 
4. Awareness about current industry expectations, career opportunities, and tips for 
succeeding in group discussions and interviews. 
Let us continue to empower students with the right guidance and skills to achieve successful careers 
and professional growth! 
The response from students was highly encouraging and overwhelming, and we look forward to 
organizing many more such career-oriented workshops in the future. 
 
 
2) Puzzles and Logical Thinking Skills 
The Student Developers Club at KIT’s College of Engineering, Kolhapur in association with ACADS, 
Department of CSE (AIML and DS) successfully conducted a one-day session on “Puzzles and Logical 
Thinking Skills” on Saturday, 04/03/2026 from 1:45 pm to 5:00 pm. 
More than 240 students benefitted from this interactive session. The event focused on enhancing 
students’ logical reasoning, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities through various 
engaging

3 
 
puzzles and brain teasers. Students enthusiastically participated in different activities that challenged 
their creativity, critical thinking, and decision-making skills. The lively atmosphere and active 
involvement of participants made the session highly engaging and enjoyable. 
A special thanks to Mr. Sujay Lande, Assistant Professor in the department of CSE (AIML) , for 
conducting the session and sharing valuable techniques to approach logical and analytical problems 
effectively. We also appreciate all the students for their energetic participation and positive 
response throughout the session. 
The participants of this session benefitted with practical exposure to different types of puzzles and 
problem-solving methods. Following are the outcomes of this session: 
1. Development of logical reasoning and analytical thinking skills through solving various puzzles 
and brain teasers. 
2. Improvement in problem-solving approaches, decision-making abilities, and creative 
thinking techniques. 
3. Enhancement of aptitude skills useful for competitive examinations, coding assessments, 
and placement preparation. 
4. Understanding the importance of patience, observation, and structured thinking while 
solving complex problems. 
Let us continue to encourage innovative thinking and problem-solving skills among students through 
such interactive and knowledge-enriching activities! 
The response from students was extremely positive and overwhelming, and we look forward to 
organizing many more such engaging and skill-oriented sessions in the future.

Information About Club: 
The Amateur Writers Club of KIT’s College of Engineering (Autonomous), Kolhapur, is a student-driven 
literary club established with the aim of promoting creativity, reading habits, and effective writing skills 
among students. The club provides a dynamic platform for aspiring writers, readers, poets, and speakers 
to express their ideas and showcase their talents through various literary and creative activities. 
The club actively organizes writing workshops, brainstorming sessions, group discussions, competitions, 
library visits, poetry recitations, and interactive author sessions to nurture literary potential among 
students. Through these activities, the club encourages  intellectual thinking, creativity, communication 
skills, and confidence among participants. 
The Amateur Writers Club also focuses on bridging the gap between creativity and technology by 
introducing students to technical and professional writing practices . The club promotes student 
engagement through official platforms and creates an environment where literature, expression, and 
innovation are appreciated. By conducting events such as Mehfil, Vachan Prerana Din, Marathi Bhasha 
Din, and Author Talks, the cl ub successfully inspires students to explore literature and  develop their

Information about club – 
The Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB) Club is an initiative to promote national integration and 
cultural unity among the states of India. The club aims to strengthen the idea of “Unity in 
Diversity” by encouraging students to learn about the traditions, languages, and cultural practices 
of different regions. 
Various activities are organized under the EBSB Club, such as cultural presentations, Modi lipi 
workshop, quizzes, poster-making, and events like Sanskruti Prabodhan, where students represent 
and showcase the uniqueness of different states. These activities help students gain knowledge 
about India’s rich cultural heritage while developing respect and appreciation for diversity. 
Participation in the club enhances students’ communication skills, creativity, and teamwork. It also 
fosters a sense of responsibility and national pride among them. 
Overall, the EBSB Club serves as an effective platform for promoting cultural awareness, mutual 
understanding, and unity among students, contributing to the development of informed and 
responsible citizens. 
 
Faculty Coordinator - Ms. Sneha Kagale

Summary of Each Activity: 
1. Avani Sanstha Visit & Independence Day : 
On 15th August 2025, the Ek Bharat Shrestha Bharat Club visited Avani Sanstha to celebrate 
Independence Day and spread joy among the children. The visit included a street play on Women 
Empowerment, an Open Mic session where students showcased their singing talents, and a creative 
workshop on making eco-friendly sky lanterns. The program featured positive interactions

4 
 
 
 
between club members, faculty, Sanstha staff, and children; Strengthening their commitment to 
the children's welfare, including a generous donation of rice, fruits and financial support. The event 
successfully created social awareness, encouraged creativity, and fostered a sense of empathy and 
community responsibility among the participants while strengthening the bond between the club 
and the Sanstha. 
 
 
 
2. Sanskruti Prabodhan Activity 
The Ek Bharat Shrestha Bharat Club of Kol hapur Institute of Technology organized Sanskruti 
Prabodhan, a cultural diversity activity aimed at spreading awareness and cultural pride among 
students. The event featured student volunteers who were assigned different states of India and 
delivered prese ntations covering culture, festivals, food, and important landmarks. It included 
engaging segments such as state -wise presentations, street skits depicting regional lifestyles, 
cultural dance performances, songs, and active audience interaction. The activi ty successfully 
provided students a firsthand experience of India’s cultural richness & boosted their confidence.

5 
 
 
 
 
3. Uttarayan - Sanskruti Sangam 
 
The opening day of Uttarayan, themed Sanskruti Sangam, served as a vibrant tribute  to India's 
diverse heritage and the spirit of collective creativity. The event commenced with a prestigious 
Inauguration Ceremony at the Kolhapur Institute of Technology, where students gathered to 
celebrate the core values of the Ek Bharat Shrestha Bhara t initiative. A major highlight of the 
morning was the Heritage Hunt, an immersive and fast -paced competition that required 
participants to solve cultural riddles and effectively blending physical activity with intellectual 
discovery. This was followed by an intensive Kite Making Activity, where students transitioned 
from being observers of tradition to active creators. Working in teams, they utilized various 
materials to design provided by team EBSB and construct their own kites, a process that not only 
fostered artistic expression but also strengthened peer bonding. 
 
 
4. Uttarayan - Ambar Utsav 
The second day, celebrated as Ambar Utsav, brought the energy of the festival to the open skies, 
focusing on the joy of participation. The day began with the highly anticipated Kite Flying session, 
where the vibrant creations from the previous day’s workshop filled the air. This activity served 
as a powerful visual representation of unity in diversity, as students from various backgrounds 
joined together in a shared cultural tradition, demonstrating both sportsmanship and coordination. 
Following the excitement on the field, the atmosphere shifted to the Open Mic Session, which 
provided an inclusive and supportive platform for students to voice their thoughts, share poe try, 
or showcase musical talents. This session was instrumental in boosting the participants' confidence 
and leadership skills, allowing them to connect on a deeper personal level and reinforcing the sense 
of community that the EBSB Club aims to cultivate within the institute.

6 
 
 
 
 
 
5. Modi Lipi Workshop 
A Modi Lipi Workshop was conducted during the Uttarayan event by the EBSB Club to create 
awareness about the historical script of Maharashtra. The workshop introduced participants to the 
origin, history, and cultural significance of Modi Lipi, which was widely used during the Maratha 
Empire for administrative purposes. It included explanations of its importance in Marathi heritage 
providing historic evidences such as temple records and manuscripts associated with temples like 
Tulja bhavani temple, demonstrations of basic alphabets and writing patterns, and an interactive 
discussion on preserving traditional scripts. The session was informative and engaging, 
successfully inspiring students to appreciate and preserve Maharashtra’s rich linguistic heritage.

7 
 
 
 
6. Stargazing activity 
During the Uttarayan event, a stargazing activity was successfully organized in collaboration with 
the Gaganvedi Team. The session aimed to spread awareness and knowledge about astronomy and 
the night sky among participants. Information about stars, constellations, planets, and various 
celestial events visible during the Uttarayan sky was shared in an interactive and engaging manner. 
Participants were also given an opportunity to observe these astronomical objects directly through 
telescopes, making the experience both educational and memorable. The activity created great 
enthusiasm among attendees and encouraged curiosity towards space science and sky observation.

Ganesh Chaturthi Celebration 2025 
Flash Mob 
Venue: KIT’s College of Engineering, Kolhapur 
Date: 28 August 2025 
Organized by: Aura Club 
Support: Cultural Committee 
 
● Introduction 
Ganesh Chaturthi, one of the most revered and traditional festivals  in India, was celebrated with 
great devotion and enthusiasm at KIT’s  College of Engineering, Kolhapur on 27 August 2025. 
The celebration aimed to honor Lord Ganesha and to promote cultural values and unity among 
students and staff members. 
 
● Event Overview 
The event was organized by the Aura Club of the college, with active  support from the Cultural 
Committee in planning and execution. The celebration commenced with the installation  of Lord 
Ganesha’s idol followed by traditional pooja and prayers. Faculty members, students, and staff 
gathered to seek blessings and participat e in the auspicious occasion, creating a spiritually 
uplifting atmosphere across the campus. 
● Cultural Performances 
A major highlight of the celebration was the vibrant flash mob performance conducted by the 
Cultural Committee members as a part of the progr am. The energetic presentation added 
excitement and brought together students in a joyful spirit. In addition, a semi -classical dance 
performance was presented, beautifully reflecting devotion and the cultural significance of 
Ganesh Chaturthi. The performe rs were appreciated for their coordination, expressions, and 
dedication. 
 
● Participation and Coordination 
The event witnessed active participation from students and faculty members. The Aura Club 
ensured proper planning and smooth execution of the celebrati on, while the Cultural Committee 
played a significant role in organizing and performing the cultural activities. 
 
● Conclusion 
The Ganesh Chaturthi celebration at KIT’s College of Engineering was conducted successfully, 
blending traditional rituals with mode rn cultural expressions. The event strengthened unity, 
promoted cultural awareness, and created a memorable experience for everyone present on 
campus.

4 
 
Youth Festival 2025–2026 
District Level and Central 
The District Level and Central Youth Festiv al for the academic year 2025 –2026 was organized 
under the guidance of Shivaji University. This prestigious festival marked the 45th Youth 
Festival of the University and was conducted in a two -stage format comprising District Level  
and Central Level competitions. 
The primary objective of the Youth Festival was to provide a dynamic platform for students to 
exhibit their artistic, literary, and cultural talents while fostering creativity, discipline, and 
healthy competition among affiliated colleges. 
 
● District Level Youth Festival 
The District Level Youth Festival was conducted at different host colleges across various  
districts as per the official schedule: 
● Satara District – 9th September 2025 
● Sangli District – 11th September 2025 
● Kolhapur District – 13th September 2025 
The competitions were organized systematically under the supervision of university authorities 
and host institutions. Students from affiliated colleges participated enthusiastically in various 
individual and group events. 
The major competitions included: 
● Debate 
● Elocution (Marathi, Hindi, and English) 
● Classical Singing (Solo) 
● Classical Group Singing 
● Quiz Competition 
● Solo Folk Instrument 
● One Act Play 
● Group Singing 
Participants demonstrated remarkable confidence, preparation, and stage presence. Expert judges 
evaluated performances based on predefined criteria, ensuring fairness and transparency. 
As per the revised structure for 2025 –2026, the District Level Festival awarded First, Second, 
Third, Fourth, and Fifth positions. The top five winners in each competition qualified to 
participate in the Central Youth Festival.

5 
 
Additionally, certain structural changes were implemented this year. The Solo Folk Instrument 
event was directly included in the Central Y outh Festival category, and a new group event 
(Shobhayatra) was introduced at the Central Level. 
 
● Central Youth Festival 
The Central Youth Festival was conducted from 18th September to 20th September 2025 at the 
designated host college. Students who secure d top positions at the district level represented their 
respective colleges at this higher stage of competition. 
The Central Festival witnessed outstanding performances and healthy inter -collegiate 
competition. Participants displayed exceptional talent in literary, performing arts, and cultural 
events. The event not only celebrated artistic excellence but also strengthened the  spirit of unity 
and collaboration among students from different districts. 
 
● Participation and Achievements 
Our college actively participated in the Youth Festival with great enthusiasm. The students 
represented the institution in multiple competitions and performed commendably. 
Notable achievements include: 
● First Prize – Quiz Competition 
● Second Prize – English Elocution 
● Consolation Prize – Solo Folk Instrument 
These accomplishments brought pride and recognition to  the institution. The dedicated efforts of 
the students, along with continuous guidance from faculty coordinators, played a vital role in 
securing these achievements.

AURA: The Energy of Art 
Establishment Year – 2012 
About Club 
 
 
AURA, the soul of artistic expression at KITCoEK, was born from a simple idea 
- to give students a space where creativity meets curiosity. More than just a club, 
AURA is a movement that celebrates the power of visual storytelling, design, 
and artistic innovation. With every brushstroke, poster, and installation, it brings 
life to the campus and a voice to the ideas that often go unspoken. 
Throughout the year, AURA channels this energy into a series of inspiring events 
that spark both conversation and imagination. Whether it’s challenging minds 
through conceptual design in Co -evolution, bringing tradition to life during the 
Ganesh Festival, reflecting inner thoughts in Darpan, or exploring the future of 
creativity in Kaladalan 2026, each initiative is a canvas of bold ideas and 
collaborative effort. 
What sets AURA apart is its belief that art is not just decoration - it’s a force. A 
force that can inspire change, question norms, and connect people. The club 
thrives on pushing boundaries by merging art with technology, sustainability, 
and innovation. It empowers students to not only create but to communicate, 
innovate, and lead. 
Behind every vibrant backdrop and powerful visual is a team of passionate minds 
- planners, painters, thinkers, and dreamers - who make the magic happen. 
AURA doesn’t just organize events; it curates experiences, creates meaning, and 
leaves behind impressions that last well beyond the final exhibit.

Description: 
On 21st August 2025 , AURA: The Energy of Art organized an engaging Design 
Workshop on Figma and Canva to introduce students to modern graphic design tools and 
enhance their creative and digital design skills. The workshop aimed to provide participants 
with practical knowledge of designing visually appealing posters, presentations, social 
media creatives, and user interface layouts using two of the most popular design platforms. 
The session began with an introduction to the fundamentals of graphic design, including 
color theory, typography, layout principles, and visual hierarchy. Participants were then 
introduced to the features and applications of Canva for quick and effective graphic design, 
followed by Figma, where they learned the basics of UI/UX design, wireframing, 
prototyping, and collaborative designing. The workshop included live demonstrations, 
hands-on activities, and inter active design exercises, allowing participants to create their 
own posters, social media posts. The trainers also shared valuable design tips, shortcuts, and 
best  practices  to  help  students  improve  their  creativity  and  workflow. 
Students actively participated throughout the workshop by asking questions, experimenting 
with design tools, and showcasing their creative outputs. The interactive learning 
environment encouraged collaboration, innovation, and confidence in using digital design 
software. 
The Design Workshop: Figma and Canva successfully equipped students with essential 
design skills relevant to academics, technical projects, competitions, and professional 
development. The event was well received by participants and marked another successfu l 
initiative by AURA: The Energy of Art in promoting creativity, innovation, and digital 
learning among students.

The celebration began with the grand Ganesh Agaman on 26th August 2025. Lord Ganesha 
was welcomed with an energetic Dhol Pathak procession, filling the campus with joy and

Description: 
KALADALAN 2026 – The Flagship Art Exhibition by AURA 
KALADALAN 2026, the flagship art exhibition organized by AURA: The Energy of Art, the Art 
Club of KIT’s College of Engineering, Kolhapur, was held from 21st February to 22nd February 
2026. Spanning two days, the exhibition brought together creativity, imagination, artistic 
expression, and social awareness under the thought -provoking theme: “Yugantara: The Human 
Shift.” 
The word Yugantara represents a transition from one era to another —a significant shift in human 
values, lifestyles, relationships, and connection with the world. Through various artworks, 
installations, and creative models, the exhibition portrayed the jo urney of humanity across four 
symbolic ages: The Age of Balance, The Age of Growth, The Age of Competition, and The Age 
of Disconnection. 
The exhibition was inaugurated with a ribbon -cutting ceremony by the esteemed guests, marking 
the beginning of a meaningful and immersive artistic journey. Each artwork encouraged visitors to 
reflect on how human civilization has evolved —from living peacefully in harmony with nature to 
experiencing rapid growth, intense competition, technological advancement, and inc reasing 
emotional and social disconnection. 
This year’s exhibition focused on presenting the transformation of human life through creative 
storytelling. Paintings, sketches, artistic installations, handcrafted models, sculptures, and 
innovative displays we re used to illustrate the changing relationship between humans, nature, 
society, technology, and emotions.

12  
The Four Ages of Yugantara: 
● The Age of Balance: 
This stage represented a time when humans lived peacefully in harmony with nature. Life was 
simple, relationships were meaningful, and people respected natural resources. The artworks 
reflected unity, balance, cultural values, and a deep connection between humanity and the 
environment. 
● The Age of Growth: 
This stage portrayed the development of human civilization through knowledge, education, 
innovation, industrialization, and technological advancement. It represented progress, creativity, 
opportunities, and humanity’s continuous desire to learn, explore, and build a better future. 
● The Age of Competition: 
This stage highlighted the growing race for success, wealth, recognition, power, and achievement. 
The artworks depicted the increasing pressure of modern life, where competition often influences 
personal choices, relationships, ambitions, and individual identity. 
● The Age of Disconnection: 
The final stage reflected the consequences of rapid technological advancement and changing 
lifestyles. Although people are digitally connected more than ever, emotional distance, loneliness, 
environmental neglect, and reduced human interaction have become growing concerns. The 
artworks encouraged visitors to reconnect with nature, society, relationships, and their inner 
selves. 
Highlights of the Exhibition Included: 
● Creative installations representing humanity’s transition through the four ages—Balance, 
Growth, Competition, and Disconnection. 
● Artistic models portraying the evolution of human civilization, society, technology, and changing 
lifestyles. 
● Thought-provoking artworks highlighting the impact of rapid technological development on 
human emotions and relationships. 
● Creative displays representing the growing distance between humans and nature in the modern 
world. 
● Paintings and sketches depicting cultural values, human emotions, social transformation, 
environmental awareness, and the changing identity of humanity. 
● Innovative models and installations demonstrating the contrast between traditional life and the 
technology-driven modern era. 
● A diverse collection of paintings, sketches, sculptures, handcrafted artworks, and creative exhibits 
showcasing the artistic talent and imagination of AURA members.

13  
At the heart of the exhibition stood the central theme, “Yugantara: The Human Shift,” 
representing humanity’ s journey through changing eras. The transition from balance to growth, 
from growth to competition, and ultimately toward disconnection encouraged visitors to reflect on 
an important question: As humanity continues to progress, are we becoming more connect ed 
or gradually losing our connection with nature, society, and ourselves? 
KALADALAN 2026 was more than an art exhibition —it was a journey through time and a 
reflection of human transformation. Through creativity and artistic expression, the exhibition 
conveyed a powerful message about balancing progress with humanity, technology with emotions, 
and development with environmental responsibility. 
The event received enthusiastic participation and appreciation from students, faculty members, 
guests, and visitors. KALADALAN 2026 marked another successful chapter in AURA’s journey 
of artistic excellence, creativity, awareness, and meaningful social expression.

Description: 
KALADALAN 2026 – The Flagship Art Exhibition by AURA 
KALADALAN 2026, the flagship art exhibition organized by AURA: The Energy of Art, the Art 
Club of KIT’s College of Engineering, Kolhapur, was held from 21st February to 22nd February 
2026. Spanning two days, the exhibition brought together creativity, imagination, artistic 
expression, and social awareness under the thought -provoking theme: “Yugantara: The Human 
Shift.” 
The word Yugantara represents a transition from one era to another —a significant shift in human 
values, lifestyles, relationships, and connection with the world. Through various artworks, 
installations, and creative models, the exhibition portrayed the jo urney of humanity across four 
symbolic ages: The Age of Balance, The Age of Growth, The Age of Competition, and The Age 
of Disconnection. 
The exhibition was inaugurated with a ribbon -cutting ceremony by the esteemed guests, marking 
the beginning of a meaningful and immersive artistic journey. Each artwork encouraged visitors to 
reflect on how human civilization has evolved —from living peacefully in harmony with nature to 
experiencing rapid growth, intense competition, technological advancement, and inc reasing 
emotional and social disconnection. 
This year’s exhibition focused on presenting the transformation of human life through creative 
storytelling. Paintings, sketches, artistic installations, handcrafted models, sculptures, and 
innovative displays we re used to illustrate the changing relationship between humans, nature, 
society, technology, and emotions. 
--- Page 13 ---
 
12  
The Four Ages of Yugantara: 
● The Age of Balance: 
This stage represented a time when humans lived peacefully in harmony with nature. Life was 
simple, relationships were meaningful, and people respected natural resources. The artworks 
reflected unity, balance, cultural values, and a deep connection between humanity and the 
environment. 
● The Age of Growth: 
This stage portrayed the development of human civilization through knowledge, education, 
innovation, industrialization, and technological advancement. It represented progress, creativity, 
opportunities, and humanity’s continuous desire to learn, explore, and build a better future. 
● The Age of Competition: 
This stage highlighted the growing race for success, wealth, recognition, power, and achievement. 
The artworks depicted the increasing pressure of modern life, where competition often influences 
personal choices, relationships, ambitions, and individual identity. 
● The Age of Disconnection: 
The final stage reflected the consequences of rapid technological advancement and changing 
lifestyles. Although people are digitally connected more than ever, emotional distance, loneliness, 
environmental neglect, and reduced human interaction have become growing concerns. The 
artworks encouraged visitors to reconnect with nature, society, relationships, and their inner 
selves. 
Highlights of the Exhibition Included: 
● Creative installations representing humanity’s transition through the four ages—Balance, 
Growth, Competition, and Disconnection. 
● Artistic models portraying the evolution of human civilization, society, technology, and changing 
lifestyles. 
● Thought-provoking artworks highlighting the impact of rapid technological development on 
human emotions and relationships. 
● Creative displays representing the growing distance between humans and nature in the modern 
world. 
● Paintings and sketches depicting cultural values, human emotions, social transformation, 
environmental awareness, and the changing identity of humanity. 
● Innovative models and installations demonstrating the contrast between traditional life and the 
technology-driven modern era. 
● A diverse collection of paintings, sketches, sculptures, handcrafted artworks, and creative exhibits 
showcasing the artistic talent and imagination of AURA members. 
--- Page 14 ---
 
13  
At the heart of the exhibition stood the central theme, “Yugantara: The Human Shift,” 
representing humanity’ s journey through changing eras. The transition from balance to growth, 
from growth to competition, and ultimately toward disconnection encouraged visitors to reflect on 
an important question: As humanity continues to progress, are we becoming more connect ed 
or gradually losing our connection with nature, society, and ourselves? 
KALADALAN 2026 was more than an art exhibition —it was a journey through time and a 
reflection of human transformation. Through creativity and artistic expression, the exhibition 
conveyed a powerful message about balancing progress with humanity, technology with emotions, 
and development with environmental responsibility. 
The event received enthusiastic participation and appreciation from students, faculty members, 
guests, and visitors. KALADALAN 2026 marked another successful chapter in AURA’s journey 
of artistic excellence, creativity, awareness, and meaningful social expression.

“Grit & Grace” “Elocution Competition” 
Date: 30th Oct 2025 
Time : 01:45 pm onwards 
Venue : Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, Electrical Seminar Hall 
The Women Development Gender Equality Cell (WDGEC) of Kolhapur Institute of Technology’s 
College of Engineering, Kolhapur, successfully organized the event “Grit and Grace” featuring an 
Elocution Competition and Poster Making Competition to promote awareness about gender 
equality, women empowerment, and social responsibility among students. The Elocution 
Competition, held on 30th October 2025, provided participants with a platform to express their 
thoughts on important topics such as women in STEM, challenging stereotypes, safeguarding the 
girl child, and ending gender-based violence. Dr. Pallavi Patil , Prof and Head , Biotech dept graced 
the occasion as the Chief guest. 
The speeches were judged and evaluated by Prof. Shruti Kashid, Professor , First yr dept. 
Number of participants : 18 
Students confidently shared impactful ideas, enhancing their communication skills and social 
awareness. The winners were announced, and they were applauded for their remarkable 
performances. Certificates and cash prizes were distributed to the winners and participants. 
 
 
“Grit & Grace” “Poster Making Competition” 
Date: 1st Nov, 2025 
Time : 01:45 pm onwards 
Venue : Seminar hall, Main Building 
The Poster Making Competition, conducted on 1st November 2025, encouraged participants to 
creatively present themes like equality, women’s voices, youth empowerment, and justice for 
women through innovative artwork and meaningful messages. Both events witnessed enthusiastic 
participation from students across departments and successfully inspired creativity, confidence, 
and sensitivity toward gender equality issues. The competitions concluded with prize distribution 
and appreciation certificates for all participants, making the event highly motivating and 
memorable for everyone involved. Dr. Pallavi Patil , Prof and Head , Biotech dept graced the 
occasion as the Chief guest and evaluated the posters. 
No of participants: 24

The winners were announced, and they were applauded for their remarkable performances. 
Certificates and cash prizes were distributed to the winners and participants. 
 
 
Seminar on “International HPV awareness day 
Date: Wednesday, 4 th March , 2026 
Venue : Seminar hall, Main Building 
The Kolhapur Medical Association (KMA) in collaboration with Kolhapur Cancer Centre (KCC) organized 
an HPV Awareness Program on the occasion of International HPV Awareness Day to spread awareness 
about the importance of HPV vaccination and cervical cancer prevention. The event, held at KIT College 
of Engineering, Kolhapur, focused on educating students and attendees about the long -term protection 
provided by the HPV vaccine and the need for early preventive healthcare measures. Dr. Reshma Pawar, 
Director of KCC, delivered an informative session highlighting the significance of HPV vaccination, 
women’s health, and cancer awareness. The program was graced by Chief Guest Dr. R. M. Kulkarni, 
President of KMA, along with other distinguished members of the association. The awareness initiative 
successfully encouraged participants to understand the importance of vaccination, preventive screening, 
and public health awareness, making the event highly educational and socially impactful. 
 
 
ABHYUDAYA 2026 “Flame-Free Flavours (Food Making Competition)” 
Date : 13th March, 2026 
Venue : Seminar hall, Main Building 
The Flame-Free Flavours (Food Making Competition), organized by the Women Development 
and Gender Equality Cell (WDGEC), provided students with an exciting platform to showcase 
their culinary creativity and innovation. The competition encouraged participants to prepare 
unique and delicious dishes without the use of fire, promoting the idea of safe and quick cooking 
methods. The event aimed to enhance students’ creativity, presentation skills, and teamwork while 
highlighting the importance of nutrition and smart cooking techniques. Participants 
enthusiastically presented a variety of innovative dishes, demonstrating their talent, imagination, 
and passion for cooking 
The winners were announced, and they were applauded for their remarkable performances. 
Certificates and cash prizes were distributed to the winners and participants. 
 
 
ABHYUDAYA 2026 - Beyond the Script (One-Act Play Competition) 
Date : 14th March 2026 
Venue : Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, Electrical Seminar Hall

6 
 
The One-Act Play Competition, organized by the Women Development and Gender Equality Cell 
(WDGEC) as part of ABHYUDAYA 2026, provided students with a dynamic platform to showcase 
their theatrical talent and social awareness. The competition encouraged participants to present 
powerful messages on gender equality and empowerment through acting, dialogue, and 
storytelling. It aimed to enhance students’ confidence, creativity, and teamwork skills while 
addressing important social issues. This event allowed students to go beyond words and express 
meaningful themes through performance, bringing ideas like equality, leadership, and social 
change to life on stage. The One-Act Play Competition was centered around four meaningful 
themes designed to encourage participants to explore deep social realities and human emotions 
through dramatic performance. Teams were required to select one of the following themes for their 
play: 
• The Silent Sacrifice: Focusing on the unnoticed struggles and sacrifices individuals make for 
their families and society. 
• The Unseen Work: Highlighting the often-unrecognized efforts, especially of women, in 
maintaining households and supporting others. 
• Generation of Change: Showcasing the role of youth in bringing positive transformation and 
challenging outdated norms. 
• Behind Every Success: Emphasizing the hidden support systems and contributions that lead to 
an individual’s achievements. 
The event concluded with a formal announcement of the winners who best captured the essence 
of ABHYUDAYA 2026. 
• Winner: Sharayu Kadam -₹2000 
• Runner-up: Madhura Patil -₹1500 
To motivate all participants, E-certificates were issued, recognizing their creative contribution to 
the Women Development and Gender Equality Cell’s initiative. 
 
 
ABHYUDAYA 2026 Creative Canvas: Painting Competition 
Date : 14th March 2026 
Venue : Seminar hall, Central Library, KITCoEK 
The Creative Canvas (Painting Competition), organized by the Women Development and Gender 
Equality Cell (WDGEC) as part of ABHYUDAYA 2026, provided students with a vibrant platform 
to showcase their artistic expression and social perspectives. The competition encouraged 
participants to translate complex themes of gender equality and empowerment into visual art. The 
event aimed to enhance students' creativity, critical thinking, and aesthetic sensibilities while 
highlighting important social messages through the medium of painting. This competition was 
designed to let students express social themes through art. The goal was to move beyond traditional

7 
 
discussions and see how students visualize concepts like leadership, gender roles, and future 
equality. The competition was centered around four specific themes designed to provoke thought 
regarding gender dynamics and the future of equality. Participants were required to choose one of 
the following for their artwork:

The Women Development Gender Equality Cell (WDGEC) of Kolhapur Institute of Technology’s 
College of Engineering, Kolhapur, successfully organized the event “Grit and Grace” featuring an 
Elocution Competition and Poster Making Competition to promote awareness about gender 
equality, women empowerment, and social responsibility among students. The Elocution 
Competition, held on 30th October 2025, provided participants with a platform to express their 
thoughts on important topics such as women in STEM, challenging stereotypes, safeguarding the 
girl child, and ending gender-based violence. Dr. Pallavi Patil , Prof and Head , Biotech dept graced 
the occasion as the Chief guest. 
The speeches were judged and evaluated by Prof. Shruti Kashid, Professor , First yr dept. 
Number of participants : 18 
Students confidently shared impactful ideas, enhancing their communication skills and social 
awareness. The winners were announced, and they were applauded for their remarkable 
performances. Certificates and cash prizes were distributed to the winners and participants. 
 
 
“Grit & Grace” “Poster Making Competition” 
Date: 1st Nov, 2025 
Time : 01:45 pm onwards 
Venue : Seminar hall, Main Building 
The Poster Making Competition, conducted on 1st November 2025, encouraged participants to 
creatively present themes like equality, women’s voices, youth empowerment, and justice for 
women through innovative artwork and meaningful messages. Both events witnessed enthusiastic 
participation from students across departments and successfully inspired creativity, confidence, 
and sensitivity toward gender equality issues. The competitions concluded with prize distribution 
and appreciation certificates for all participants, making the event highly motivating and 
memorable for everyone involved. Dr. Pallavi Patil , Prof and Head , Biotech dept graced the 
occasion as the Chief guest and evaluated the posters. 
No of participants: 24

Seminar on “International HPV awareness day 
Date: Wednesday, 4 th March , 2026 
Venue : Seminar hall, Main Building 
The Kolhapur Medical Association (KMA) in collaboration with Kolhapur Cancer Centre (KCC) organized 
an HPV Awareness Program on the occasion of International HPV Awareness Day to spread awareness 
about the importance of HPV vaccination and cervical cancer prevention. The event, held at KIT College 
of Engineering, Kolhapur, focused on educating students and attendees about the long -term protection 
provided by the HPV vaccine and the need for early preventive healthcare measures. Dr. Reshma Pawar, 
Director of KCC, delivered an informative session highlighting the significance of HPV vaccination, 
women’s health, and cancer awareness. The program was graced by Chief Guest Dr. R. M. Kulkarni, 
President of KMA, along with other distinguished members of the association. The awareness initiative 
successfully encouraged participants to understand the importance of vaccination, preventive screening, 
and public health awareness, making the event highly educational and socially impactful.

methods. The event aimed to enhance students’ creativity, presentation skills, and teamwork while 
highlighting the importance of nutrition and smart cooking techniques. Participants

EVENT REPORT -A.Y.2025-26  
 
 
Name of Club – Society of Women Engineers (SWE), Kolhapur Affiliate  
Logo –  
 
 
Tagline :  
  Establishment Year- 2025 
 
Information about club – 
The Society of Women Engineers (SWE) is a globally recognized non-profit organization that inspires 
women to achieve their full potential as engineers, leaders, and innovators. At KIT’s College of 
Engineering (Empowered Autonomous), Kolhapur (KITCOEK) , the SWE chapter has consistently 
worked towards empowering female students through various events that promote technical knowledge, 
leadership qualities, and communication skills. 
We at SWE Kolhapur Affiliate dedicated to address diverse aspects for existence and survival of the fittest 
, organized various activities. 
 
Faculty Coordinator - Ms. Sushnmita Sarkar

2 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1. Introduction to the Society of Women Engineers (SWE) 
The Intercollegiate Debate Competition, a flagship event of SWE, was conceptualized to 
encourage logical thinking, analytical reasoning, and confidence among students. It aimed not only 
to polish their oratory skills but also to promote healthy discussions on diverse topics relevant to 
society, technology, and philosophy. 
2. Commencement and Design of the Event 
The event commenced with great enthusiasm in the seminar hall, which was 
beautifully adorned with thematic posters and banners designed by the SWE student 
team. The stage setup reflected professionalism and creativity, featuring the SWE 
logo, podiums for the debaters, and a well-arranged seating area for dignitaries, 
judges, and participants. 
The debate competition was designed in three rounds, each testing the depth of 
participants’ knowledge, their spontaneity, and their ability to reason under pressure. The 
structure was carefully planned to allow both individual and group debates, ensuring a 
dynamic and engaging flow throughout the day. 
 
 
3. Inauguration and Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony 
The inaugural session began with the entry of the esteemed chief guests – Mrs. Sharanya 
Menon and Mr. Soham Tiwade. The audience welcomed them with thunderous applause an 
warmth. The inauguration was symbolized by a ribbon-cutting ceremony, signifying the official 
commencement of the event. 
Following the inauguration, the guests were presented with floral bouquets and words of 
appreciation by the SWE coordinators and student representatives. 
 
 
4. Introduction  of the Guests Mrs. Sharanya Menon 
Mrs. Menon is a distinguished educator and mentor known for her remarkable contribution to 
communication and personality development programs. With years of experience in teaching 
and training, she has guided countless students to excel in professional and leadership arenas. 
Her calm demeanor and inspiring personality made her presence truly enriching for the event. 
Mr. Soham Tiwade 
Mr. Soham Tiwade is a young orator, engineer, and critical thinker known for his 
innovative insights into philosophy and technology. His educational background blends 
analytical rigor with creative

3 
 
thought, making him a dynamic speaker. His enthusiasm for student development 
and open-mindedness towards diverse perspectives made him a perfect guest for the 
debate competition. 
 
5. Exchange of Tokens of Appreciation 
 
As a gesture of goodwill, Mrs. Sharanya Menon presented a token of appreciation to 
Mr. Soham Tiwade, symbolizing collaboration and mutual respect. 
In turn, Mrs. Sarkar, the Head Faculty Coordinator of SWE at KITCOEK, presented 
a token of gratitude to Mrs. Sharanya Menon for gracing the event with her presence 
and words of wisdom. 
 
Another highlight was the presentation of a token to Judge Mrs. Shruti Kashid by 
Mrs. Jahida Khan, Co-Faculty Coordinator of SWE, recognizing her contribution and 
support to the competition.

4 
 
6. Address by the Dignitaries 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Speech by Mrs. Sarkar (Head Faculty Coordinator, SWE) 
Mrs. Sarkar opened the event with a warm and thoughtful speech. She highlighted the 
purpose of organizing the debate — to provide a platform for young minds to express their 
viewpoints fearlessly and responsibly. Reflecting on Mrs. Sharanya Menon’s extensive 
experience, she emphasized the importance of confidence, preparation, and respect in public 
discourse. Her words set a positive and encouraging tone for the day. 
Speech by Mrs. Sharanya Menon 
Mrs. Menon, in her address, beautifully spoke about enthusiasm, empowerment, and 
equality for women in all domains. She motivated students to use their voices as 
instruments of change and to uphold respect in debates as in real life. She expressed her 
admiration for the energy of the participants and congratulated the SWE team for 
providing such a meaningful platform. 
Speech by Mr. Soham Tiwade 
Mr. Tiwade began his speech with a striking thought of disagreement by Stephen 
Hawking, transitioning into examples such as the death of George Washington due to 
misinformation, the discrimination faced by Rosa Parks, and insights from Advaita 
philosophy. He skillfully interlinked these points to explain how disagreement, 
awareness, and philosophical reasoning are central to debate and progress. 
He concluded his thought-provoking speech by appreciating all participants for being part 
of a journey where ideas, not egos, are tested.

5 
 
 
7. Structure and Rules of the Debate 
The debate competition was structured to test the articulation, spontaneity, and reasoning 
of the participants under defined time limits: 
 Total Duration: 9 minutes per participant/team 
o 2 minutes for preparation 
o 5 minutes for active debating 
o 2 minutes for conclusion 
There were two main categories: 
1. Individual Debate – One participant speaking for the motion and another against it. 
2. Group Debate – Four members per group, debating on topics decided by a 
coin toss to ensure impartiality. 
 
8. Round 1: Individual Debate / Group Debate

6 
 
The first round saw intense yet respectful exchanges as participants presented their 
perspectives with clarity and conviction. Each debater was judged based on content, 
logical reasoning, body language, presentation skills, and voice modulation. 
The session was judged by Mrs. Shruti Kashid , who offered keen observations on 
each debater’s command over language and confidence. Participants demonstrated 
diverse ideologies, and their balanced arguments made it an intellectually stimulating 
start. 
 
9. Round 2: Group Debate 
The second round featured group debates consisting of four members each. A toss of coin 
determined the team’s stance — for or against the motion. The interaction between teams was 
 
lively, full of critical analysis, counter-questions, and strategic rebuttals. 
This round was judged by Mrs. Kshitija Tashi , who evaluated teams on coordination, clarity of points, 
logical flow, and teamwork . Out of numerous participants, 10 groups and 8 individuals qualified for this 
round. 
Later, the individuals were divided into two groups, and the debate continued with even greater 
intensity. Dominance, rebuttal clashes, and misconceptions were handled deftly by the participants, 
leading to engaging rounds that displayed true debating spirit.

7 
 
 
1. Round 3: The Final Showdown 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
2. Valedictory Ceremony

8 
 
 
After rigorous selection, 6 groups advanced to the final round. The competition reached its 
intellectual peak as participants battled ideas with precision, supported by factual reasoning and 
passionate delivery. Judges carefully assessed the depth of arguments, counter-points, and 
concluding remarks to determine the winners. 
At the end of the final round, results were declared: 
 Winner (1st Place) 
 1st Runner-up 
 2nd Runner-up 
 Best Speaker Award 
The audience erupted with applause as winners were announced, celebrating their excellence and 
composure throughout the competition. 
The valedictory session marked the graceful conclusion 
of the event. The guest of honor, Mr. Jitendra Bhatt, 
Dean of Student Activities at KITCOEK, presided 
over the ceremony. He was welcomed by Mrs. Sarkar, 
who presented a token of appreciation on behalf of 
SWE. 
The prize distribution ceremony followed, where 
winners received certificates, trophies, and words of 
encouragement from the dignitaries. The hall resonated 
with pride and achievement as students celebrated their 
success.

9 
 
 
3. Closing Remarks and Reflections 
Both judges – Mrs. Shruti Kashid and Mrs. 
Kshitija Tashi – shared their insights and 
reflections on the overall performance of 
participants. They praised the clarity of 
thought, confidence, and respectful debating 
etiquette displayed by the students. 
In her closing note, Mrs. Sarkar expressed 
heartfelt gratitude to all guests, judges, faculty 
coordinators, and student volunteers for 
making the event a grand success. She 
acknowledged the efforts of the organizing 
committee and emphasized the importance of 
such platforms in nurturing leadership and 
communication among youth. 
 
4. Conclusion 
The Intercollegiate Debate Competition by SWE concluded on a high note, leaving an 
enduring impression of intellect, empowerment, and collaboration. The event stood as a 
shining example of the SWE mission — to inspire, empower, and unite women in 
engineering and beyond through excellence in communication and leadership. 
As participants departed, the spirit of debate, respect for differing opinions, and 
enthusiasm for learning lingered — marking yet another milestone in the journey of SWE 
at KITCOEK.

10 
 
 
 
 
EVENT 1: Guest Lecture on “Design and Application Of Analog Circuits in Modern 
Electronic Systems” 
 
On 15th of March 2026, the students club by the name “Society Of Women Engineers SWE”, Kolhapur 
Affiliate in association with Department of Electrical Engineering at Kolhapur Institute of Technology’s, 
College of Engineering, Empowered Autonomous, organized guest lecture on “Design and Application Of 
Analog Circuits in Modern Electronic Systems”. The expert lecture was delivered by Dr.Moumita Saha, 
Assistant Professor Senior Grade 1 at School Of Electronics Engineering (SENSE),VIT-AP University. 
The event witnessed enthusiastic participants from diverse Engineering branches. 
Mrs. Sushmita A. Sarkar ,SWE Kolhapur Affiliate Coordinator hosted the event.

12 
 
EVENT 2: Guest Lecture “Biodiversity of Western Ghats” 
 
A guest lecture on the topic “Biodiversity of Western Ghats” was organized for the students of Second 
Year B. Tech Civil and Environmental Engineering at KIT's College of Engineering under the banner of the 
Society of Women Engineers (SWE). The session was conducted on 08 May 2026 11:45 a.m. to 1:45 p.m. 
The activity was coordinated by Dr. Manjussa N. Sarnobbat, Departmental SWE Coordinator, 
Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. The department received valuable support and 
guidance from Dr. Akash Anand, Head of the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, in 
organizing the guest lecture successfully. The resource person for the session was Dr. Makarand Aitawade. 
He is currently working as Assistant Professor and Head in the Department of Botany at Dr. N. D. Patil 
Mahavidyalaya and possesses 16 years of teaching and research experience in the field of Botany and 
Biodiversity studies. During the lecture, Dr. Aitawade explained the rich biodiversity of the Western Ghats 
in a very engaging and informative manner. He highlighted the importance of conservation of flora and 
fauna and shared valuable insights about rare and endemic species found in the region. He has described 
six new species belonging to genera such as Mucuna and Begonia. He has also published 22 research 
papers, 44 books, and 72 general articles in newspapers and magazines. In addition, he has delivered 
expert talks on Akashvani Kolhapur. The session became highly interactive and interesting as the speaker 
presented photographs of rare flowers and videos of birds from the Western Ghats region. Students 
enthusiastically participated in the session and gained knowledge about ecological diversity, environmental 
conservation, and the significance of preserving natural ecosystems. The lecture proved to be highly 
beneficial for the students of Civil and Environmental Engineering as it enhanced their awareness 
regarding biodiversity conservation and environmental sustainability. The students appreciated the 
informative presentation and enjoyed the session thoroughly. The Department of Civil and Environmental 
Engineering expressed sincere gratitude to Dr. Makarand Aitawade for sharing his valuable knowledge and 
making the session memorable and inspiring for the students.

14 
 
EVENT 3: Guest Lecture on the topic “Art of Living” 
 
The Department of Biotechnology, in association with the Society of Women Engineers (SWE) 
Kolhapur 
Affiliate, successfully organized a Guest Lecture on the topic “Art of Living” on 15th May 2026 from 4:00 
PM to 5:00 PM at the Department of Biotechnology, KIT’s College of Engineering, Kolhapur. The 
activity was coordinated by Miss Sayali Kedam , Departmental SWE Coordinator, Department of 
Biotechnology. 
The session was conducted by Ms. Dimple Gajwani, Art of Living International Faculty, Life Coach, 
Mindfulness Trainer, Meditation Teacher, and Corporate Trainer. Mrs. Minal Dipak Chougule 
Ma’am graced the occasion with her presence. Also ,SWE Kolhapur Affiliate Coordinator Mrs. 
Sushmita A. Sarkar along with Head Department of Biotechnology, Faculty members and students 
enthusiastically participated in the session. 
The primary objective of the lecture was to create awareness about the importance of mental well-being, 
mindfulness, emotional balance, stress management, and maintaining a healthy lifestyle in today’s fast-
paced academic and professional environment. The session emphasized the significance of inner peace, 
positive thinking, concentration, and self-discipline in achieving both personal and professional growth. 
Ms. Dimple Gajwani conducted the session in a highly interactive and engaging manner. She actively 
interacted with the students and faculty members and encouraged everyone to participate in various 
mindfulness and breathing activities. The session included breathing exercises, concentration techniques, 
meditation practices, and relaxation activities that helped participants experience calmness, focus, and 
mental clarity. 
One of the major highlights of the program was the introduction to Sudarshan Kriya and its benefits in 
reducing stress, improving emotional stability, increasing concentration, and enhancing overall well-
being. The speaker explained the importance of practicing such techniques regularly to maintain mental 
and physical health. All the participants enthusiastically followed the instructions and actively 
performed the practices demonstrated during the session. 
The lecture created a positive and energetic atmosphere in the department. The participants found the 
session highly informative, inspiring, and beneficial. The interactive activities and practical demonstrations 
helped everyone understand the importance of mindfulness and healthy living in daily life.The program 
concluded with a vote of thanks expressing sincere gratitude to Ms. Dimple Gajwani for her valuable 
guidance and inspiring interaction. Sincere gratitude was expressed to 
Dr. Pallavi Patil , Head Department of Biotechnology.

16 
 
EVENT 5: Guest Lecture on “Android App Development” 
 
The Department of Computer Science & Engineering, in association with the Society of Women 
Engineers (SWE) Kolhapur Affiliate and Computer Society Of India, successfully organized a Guest 
Lecture on the topic “Android App Development” on 16th May 2026 from 5:00 PM to 6:30 PM in 
online mode at KIT’s College of Engineering, Kolhapur. The activity was coordinated by Dr. Sonal 
Ayare , Departmental SWE Coordinator, Department of Computer Science & Engineering.

17 
 
EVENT 6: Guest Lecture on ”Financial Literacy for Women” 
 
The Department of Mechanical Engineering, in association with the Society of Women Engineers (SWE) 
Kolhapur Affiliate and Mechanical Engineering Students Ladies Association (MESLA), successfully 
organized a Guest Lecture on the topic “Financial Literacy for Women ” on 20th May 2026 from 
4:00 PM to 5:00 PM in online mode at KIT’s College of Engineering, Kolhapur. The activity was 
coordinated by Dr. Vinita Mane , Departmental SWE Coordinator, Department of Mechanical 
Engineering. 
 
 
 
Society Of Women Engineers SWE, is a global forum which is centered around a passion for our 
members success and continues to evolve with the challenges and opportunities, reflected in today’s 
exciting engineering and technology specialties. Society Of Women Engineers, acts as a catalyst in 
empowering women to achieve their full potential in careers as engineers and leaders; expand the image of 
the engineering and technology professions as a positive force in improving the quality of life, and 
demonstrate the value of diversity and inclusion. 
For more than seven decades, SWE has given women engineers a 
unique place and voice within the engineering industry. The session focused on analog circuits basics in 
accordance with power electronics contributing towards design applications. It was an interactive 
session backed by quiz and questionnaires where the participants were clarified with their doubts. 
 
Mrs. Sushmita A. Sarkar ,SWE Kolhapur Affiliate Coordinator proposed vote of thanks in which she 
expressed gratitude towards the management of KIT Chairman Shri Sunil Kulkarni, Vice Chairman Shri

18 
 
Sajid Hudli, Secretary Shri Dipak Chougule, Director Dr. Mohan B. Vanarotti. A special mention was 
made for Ms. Sharanya Menon, President of SWE Kolhapur Affiliate & Menon Pistons Ltd. for 
associating with Society Of Women Engineers, SWE. 
 
 
 
 
Mrs. Sushmita A. Sarkar 
SWE Kolhapur Affiliate Coordinator 
KIT’s College of Engineering (Empowered Autonomous), Kolhapur

positive thinking, concentration, and self-discipline in achieving both personal and professional growth.

mental clarity. 
One of the major highlights of the program was the introduction to Sudarshan Kriya and its benefits in 
reducing stress, improving emotional stability, increasing concentration, and enhancing overall well-
being. The speaker explained the importance of practicing such techniques regularly to maintain mental 
and physical health. All the participants enthusiastically followed the instructions and actively

Sprinters 2025 
Sprinters is a series of soft skill and personality development sessions specially designed 
and curated for First Year students. Guiding students to improve their personality and soft 
skills has always been the core motive of Sprinters. 
Sprinters is a lecture series along with personality development activities for first year 
students to enhance soft skills. We introduce topics like Presentation skills, Interview skills, 
Resume building, etc. We also conduct activities through which students learn to develop 
confidence, presentation skills, communication skills and networking. 
From 2019-20 we have also started introducing technical workshops for first year students. 
Workshops cover topics like graphics designing using Corel draw, Python, web designing, 
etc. We also conduct competition based on the workshops. We conduct these workshops to 
boost engagement and enthusiasm of the students in these workshops. 
The main motive for introducing technical sessions along with soft skill sessions is to make 
students equally strong with technical knowledge and give them a sneak -peek with the 
latest technology trends in engineering.
