Day 1: Ignite the core 
The first day of the "Sprinter s" event, themed "Spark the Vision," set the stage for an 
enriching and inspiring experience for all participants. The day was meticulously crafted 
to balance informative sessions, interactive activities, and skill-building exercises, creating 
an ideal mix of learning and engagement. 
The event kicked off with an opening ceremony, led by the respected Dean of Student 
Activities, Dr. Jitendra Bhat. Throughout the day, the dedicated core team of WWW 
facilitated the sessions, ensuring a smooth and impactful experience for all attendees. This 
ceremony marked the start of an exciting journey, instilling a sense of purpose and 
enthusiasm for the sessions to come. 
The day's first session, titled "Wealth Wisdom," highlighted the importance of financial 
literacy in both personal and professional life. The session, conducted by Sanyam Patil, 
Shivani More, and Arya Potdar, delved into money management, savings, investments, and 
financial planning. To enhance engagement, participants took part in interactive 
discussions aimed at understanding practical financial concepts, promoting awareness and 
practical application of the skills learned. 
The second session, titled "Communication Skills," focused on the significance of effective 
communication in academic and professional environments. The session, conducted by 
Pratik Kumbar, Ismail Munshi, Arya Bendre, and Samarjeet Shinde, explored various types 
of communication, covering verbal, non-verbal, and written forms, along with strategies to 
overcome communication barriers. Participants were introduced to practical techniques for 
improving their communication abilities. The session wrapped up with games and activities 
designed to improve communication and interpersonal skills. 
The final session of the day, called "Navigating Engineering Education," was designed 
specifically for first-year engineering students, many of whom are just starting their journey 
into the technical field. This session, conducted by Swayam Budhale, Samany u Patil, 
Ankita Gidde, and Sanyukta Patil, offered a roadmap for the four-year engineering journey, 
addressing key topics like academic planning, skill development, internships, and career 
preparation strategies. The goal was to provide participants with t he knowledge and 
resources they need to effectively begin their engineering education. 
Day 1 of "Sprinters" was a huge success, leaving participants feeling motivated 
and well-informed. The mix of sessions, interactive games, and practical takeaways made 
sure everyone walked away with a sense of accomplishment and enthusiasm for the next 
day.

Day 2: Trail Beyond the Horizon 
The second and final day of "Sprinters 2025," themed "Sprint to Discover," was the most 
dynamic and eventful day of the event, leaving a lasting impression on all participants. The 
day was thoughtfully organized to strike a perfect balance between activities, sessions, and 
inspiring talks, making it a well-rounded and unforgettable experience. 
The day kicked off with a lively and engaging treasure hunt aimed at fostering teamwork 
and strategic thinking among the participants. Divided into smaller groups, participants 
navigated through a series of clues and challenges scattered throughout the venue. This 
activity not only served as an icebreaker but also encouraged collaboration and critical 
thinking under time constraints. The treasure hunt created a vibrant and energetic 
atmosphere, setting the tone for the rest of the day's activities. 
After the treasure hunt, participants enjoyed a break and refreshments were provided. This 
informal session allowed everyone to exchange ideas and share experiences from the 
previous day, further strengthening the connections made during the event. 
Following the break , the core team members of WWW held an engaging session called 
"Four Years of Engineering." This session, conducted by Soham Shinde, Yashraj Chavan, 
and Tejas Aalavani, laid out a detailed roadmap for students embarking on their 
engineering journey, addres sing key topics like the dos and don'ts, how to balance 
extracurricular activities with studies, and tips for personal and professional development. 
The session's interactive format, featuring discussions and Q&A segments, helped 
participants gain a solid understanding of how to maximize their experience in engineering. 
The event also featured speeches delivered by the Event Head, Vice Head, Faculty 
Coordinator, and the Principal, who shared their insights and congratulated the participants 
for their enthusiasm. The event concluded on a high note with the announcement of the 
Treasure Hunt winners and the Best Participant awards. 
The highlight of the day was an inspiring session by the guest, Mr. Yatish Shah, General 
Manager of Sakal Media's Western Mah arashtra Division, who brought with him twenty 
years of valuable banking experience.

Guest: Mr. Yatish Shah 
Mr. Yatish Shah began his speech by sharing insights from his extensive banking and 
media experience, reflecting on the opportunities and accessibility that students have today 
compared to previous generations. He spoke about his twenty years of experience in the 
banking sector and his current role at Sakal Media. Addressing life's pivotal moments, he 
emphasized the significance of continuous learning and how to navigate one's career 
effectively. 
Mr. Shah emphasized that success comes from a combination of consistent hard work, right 
direction, and self -confidence. He urged students to become self -reliant financially, 
emotionally, and intellectually. He stated, "Success is achieved through continuous hard 
work, proper direction, and self -confidence. Become financially, emotionally, and 
intellectually self-reliant." 
Stressing the importance of productive activities, Mr. Shah advised students to invest their 
time wisely. He encouraged them to spend time learning new skills, reading, or gaining 
practical experience rather than wasting time on social media. He said, "Instead of wasting 
time on social media, invest your time in learning new skills, reading, or gaining practical 
experience. Focus on activities that contribute to your personal and professional growth." 
Mr. Shah also spoke about the importance of holistic personality development. He advised 
students not to focus solely on academic studies but to develop a multidimensional 
personality through sports, cultural programs, and social service. He noted that well -
rounded individuals are better prepared for life's challenges. 
Highlighting time as the most valuable resource, Mr. Shah stated, "Time is the most 
valuable asset. Plan each day and work with clear priorities." He stressed the importance 
of time management, planning, and prioritizing tasks to make the most of available time. 
Additionally, Mr. Shah urged students to become good team players, emphasizing that 
collaboration and teamwork are essential skills in both professional and personal life. He 
praised the field of engineering as one that promotes problem -solving and innovation, 
stressing the importance of building trust as a foundation for both personal and professional 
success. 
In his concluding remarks, Mr. Shah told the students, "Don't just become engineers, 
become good human beings. Give something back to society and preserve  your values 
along with success." This message emphasized the importance of character, ethics, and 
social responsibility alongside professional achievement, inspiring the audience to focus 
on holistic development and making meaningful contributions to society.

Abhigyan 2025 
Abhigyan, a legacy of past 13 years, is the flagship event of the Walk With World Club, 
aimed at fostering intellectual growth, leadership qualities, and career awareness among 
students. With the motto ‘By the students, For the Students’, 13th Edition of Abhigyan, 
was successfully conducted at Anand Bhavan, CSIBER, Kolhapur, bringing together an 
exceptional lineup of speakers from diverse professional backgrounds including public 
policy, entrepreneurship, media, entertainment, technology, and defence. 
The event was designed to provide students with real -world insights, motivational 
guidance, and a broader understanding of career opportunities. Through interactive 
sessions and inspiring talks, the speakers shared their journeys, challenges, and 
achievements, leaving a lasting impact on the audience. 
The primary objectives of Abhigyan 2025 are to inspire students through real -life 
success stories, provide exposure to diverse career paths and industries , promote 
innovation, leadership, and critical thinking , to guide students in adapting to 
emerging global trends and to motivate youth towards personal and professional 
excellence. 
 
The event commenced with an insightful session by Dr. Sundeep Waslekar, President 
of Strategic Foresight Group. He shared his inspiring journey from his early childhood

entrepreneurship, innovation, and the importance of staying updated with technological

of Kolhapur Institute of Technology’s College of Engineering (Autonomous), stood as a beacon 
of student-driven intellectual leadership. Spanning three days — 11th to 13th April 2026 — the 
event brought together aspiring diplomats, debaters, policy enthusiasts, and creative writers 
under one roof to engage in simulated parliamentary and international committee sessions. With 
the tagline “Poise | Accord | Emanation” and the empowering mes sage “Your Opinion 
Matters!”, the event not only echoed the voices of tomorrow's changemakers but also polished 
their leadership, diplomacy, and problem-solving capabilities. 
Backed by experienced faculty coordinators, esteemed patrons, and a passionate st udent 
organizing team, KITMUN 2026 was executed with high precision, collaborative enthusiasm, 
and a commitment to quality deliberation.

THE COMMITTEES & AGENDAS 
KITMUN 2026 featured four distinct committees , each meticulously designed to address 
critical global and local concerns. The delegates participated in structured debates and drafting 
of resolutions, immersing themselves in real-world problems and solutions. 
1. United Nations Security Council (UNSC) 
 
 
Agenda: Deliberation on Recent Extraterritorial Military Operations, Cross-Border Coercive 
Aggression, Strategic Force Posturing, and Their Implications for International Peace, State

REPORT OF VISIT OF FLYING OFFICER A VISHKAR DONGALE 
FOR INTERACTIVE SESSION CONDUCTED IN KOLHAPUR 
INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY’S COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING, 
KOLHAPUR (EMPOWERED AUTONOMOUS). 
 
Titled as:VISIT OF FLYING OFFICER A VISHKAR DONGALE 
 
Introduction: On1 April 2025 the National Cadet Corps (NCC) organized a special 
 event to welcome Flying Officer Avishkar Dongale ,who visited the college. The event 
` took place at Kit’s college of engineering (Seminar hall) , and it was attended by NCC 
 cadets, college staff, and students. 
 
The event at Kolhapur Institute of Technology College of Engineering 
Kolhapur(Empowered Autonomous) aimed to inspire cadets and students by 
sharing real-life defence experiences and  encouraged cadets to follow their 
passion, stay focused, and serve the nation with pride. 
As a part of the program, the event was divided into three main segments: 
 Interactive session with guest 
 Speech by flying officer 
 Question–Answer session with participants 
 
The event left a lasting impact on the audience, igniting a deeper sense of patriotism 
 and a clearer vision of what it means to serve the nation.  
 Flying Officer Dongale’s insights into military life, leadership, and discipline deeply 
 resonated with the cadets. 
 
 
Schedule: 
1545 HRS – Gathering at Seminar Hall 
1545–1550 HRS – Program Introduction 
1550–1600 HRS – Guest Introduction and Felicitation 
1600–1730 HRS – Speech & Interactive Session with the Officer 
1730–1745 HRS – Summary

Co-ordinator – CTO. Mr. Ranjit Patil Sir.

Agenda:To inspire and motivate students by providing valuable insights into the life, 
 values, and career journey of a Flying Officer. The session aims to instill a sense of 
 patriotism, discipline, and dedication among the youth. Through direct interaction with 
 a serving officer, students will gain a deeper understanding of the challenges, 
 responsibilities, and honour associated with a career in the armed forces. The event 
 also seeks to encourage students to develop leadership qualities, a strong sense of 
 national pride, and an interest in serving the nation through defence services or other 
 meaningful contributions. By showcasing real-life experiences and the personal 
 growth achieved through military service, the session aspires to ignite passion, courage, 
 and purpose in the minds of future leaders. 
 
Key Activities: 
 
 Speech & Guest Interaction: 
 Following a warm welcome and formal introduction, an interactive session was held 
 with Flying Officer Avishkar Dongale, which quickly became the highlight of the 
 event. A special “101 Session” was conducted exclusively for the NCC cadets, 
 designed to provide a closer look into the life of an Air Force officer.  
During this session, cadets actively engaged with the guest, asking a wide range of 
 thoughtful questions covering topics such as daily life in the armed forces, rigorous 
 training routines, career pathways, and the psychological and physical demands of 
 military service. 
Flying Officer Dongale responded with great enthusiasm and clarity, offerin g not only 
 factual insights but also personal anecdotes that resonated deeply with the young 
 audience. The officer's approachable demeanor and genuine passion for service created

a motivating atmosphere, leaving the cadets feeling inspired to push their  limits, 
 embrace discipline, and aim for excellence in all areas of life.  
 
 
 Motivational Speech by Flying Officer: 
In the next segment, Flying Officer Avishkar Dongale delivered a powerful and  
 heartfelt speech, focusing on their personal journey into the Indian Air Force. The  
 officer spoke candidly about the initial struggles, the rigorous selection process, and 
 the unwavering commitment required to overcome challenges along the way.  
Through vivid storytelling, the officer shared real-life experiences from training, field 
 duties, and moments that tested both physical endurance and mental strength. The core 
 message centered on the importance of perseverance, discipline, and purpose—
 qualities essential not just for a career in the defence forces but in any path of life.  
The speech was not only informative but emotionally uplifting, reinforcing the idea 
 that with hard work, dedication, and belief in oneself, no goal is out of reach. The 
 Flying Officer concluded with a call to action, urging cadets and students to remain 
 committed to their dreams, uphold national pride, and consider serving the nation as a 
 noble and fulfilling calling.

Conclusion: The visit of Flying Officer Avishkar Dongale was a great success and 
 proved to be a valuable learning experience for all present. It offered NCC cadets a 
 rare chance to interact with a serving defence officer and gain firsthand insight into life 
 in the Indian Air Force. 
The officer’s words inspired many cadets to work harder in their training and seriously 
 consider a future in the armed forces. The session not only motivated students but also 
 reinforced the core NCC values of discipline, leadership, and patriotism.  
Overall, the event left a lasting impact, encouraging cadets to stay focused, aim high, 
 and serve the nation with pride.

Agenda: Provide an overview of the Services Selection Board (SSB) interview, 
explaining its purpose, significance, and the various entry routes such as NDA, 
CDS, AFCAT, and TES. 
 
detailed explanation of the five-day selection process, including Stage I 
Screening Tests (OIR and PP&DT), Stage II Psychological Assessments (TAT, 
WAT, SRT, and Self-Description), Group Testing Officer (GTO) tasks over 
Days 3 and 4 (Group Discussion, Group Planning Exercise, Progressive Group 
Task, Lecturette, Command Task, and others), and the Day 5 Conference 
procedure with decision-making criteria 
 
offering practical preparation strategies to develop Officer-Like Qualities 
(OLQs), improve communication skills, enhance physical fitness, and strengthen 
psychological readiness. Common myths and mistakes will be addressed to help 
aspirants avoid pitfalls in the selection process.

Key Activities: 
 
 
 Guidance of Screnning Test(1st Day) of SSB: The Screening Test in the 
SSB, conducted on Day 1, serves as the primary shortlisting stage to filter 
candidates for further assessment and comprises two main components: 
the Officer Intelligence Rating (OIR) test and the Picture Perception and 
Discussion Test (PP&DT). The OIR test evaluates a candidate’s basic 
reasoning ability through verbal and non-verbal questions such as series 
completion, coding-decoding, analogies, pattern recognition, and figure 
classification, requiring both speed and accuracy to secure a high score. 
The PP&DT begins with the projection of a blurred picture for 30 
seconds, after which candidates are given four minutes to note the 
number of characters, their age, gender, and mood, and to craft a short, 
logical story depicting a situation, the actions taken, and a positive 
outcome. This is followed by an individual narration of the story and a 
group discussion aimed at forming a common version, where assessors 
observe clarity of thought, confidence, listening skills, teamwork, and 
leadership. Success in the Screening Test depends on sharp observation, 
original and practical storytelling, effective time management, and the 
ability to participate actively yet harmoniously in group discussions. 
Candidates should avoid unrealistic or overly dramatic plots, dominating 
or remaining silent in discussions, and neglecting easy OIR questions in 
favor of difficult ones. Regular practice with OIR question sets, timed 
story-writing from random images, and confident narration drills can 
significantly enhance performance and improve the chances of clearing 
this crucial first hurdle.

 Guidance for Psychology Test  :  The Psychology Test in the SSB, 
conducted on Day 2, is designed to assess a candidate’s personality, 
thought process, and Officer-Like Qualities (OLQs) at the subconscious 
level, without the influence of rehearsed responses. It comprises four key 
assessments.  
 
The Thematic Apperception Test (TAT) presents 11 pictures and one 
blank slide, each shown for 30 seconds, with four minutes allotted to 
write a story reflecting a positive, logical, and action-oriented approach. 
 
The Word Association Test (WAT) displays 60 words, each for 15 
seconds, requiring the candidate to form the first sentence that comes to 
mind, revealing personal attitudes and values. 
 
 The Situation Reaction Test (SRT) provides 60 real-life situations to be 
answered in 30 minutes, focusing on quick, practical, and constructive 
decision-making under pressure.  
 
The Self-Description (SD) Test asks candidates to write perceptions 
about themselves from the viewpoints of parents, teachers, friends, and 
self, along with their life goals.  
 
Performance in these tests hinges on spontaneity, honesty, and 
consistency, as assessors cross-check responses across different 
exercises. To excel, candidates should cultivate positive thinking, 
practice timed drills for each test type, and develop problem-solving 
approaches that are realistic yet optimistic, ensuring that their responses 
naturally reflect the qualities expected of a future officer.

 Guidance for Personal Interview : The Personal Interview in the SSB 
is an in-depth, one-on-one interaction between the candidate and the 
Interviewing Officer (IO), typically conducted on Day 2, 3, or 4, and is 
aimed at assessing the candidate’s personality, life experiences, 
communication skills, and Officer-Like Qualities (OLQs).  
 
The interview usually begins with a warm introduction and light 
conversation to put the candidate at ease, followed by a series of 
questions covering personal background, academics, family, hobbies, 
achievements, and current affairs.  
 
The IO often uses a detailed questionnaire known as the Personal 
Information Questionnaire (PIQ), which candidates fill out on arrival, to 
frame questions that explore consistency, honesty, and self-awareness. 
Situational and opinion-based questions are asked to evaluate decision-
making, responsibility, and adaptability, while rapid-fire rounds test 
memory, clarity of thought, and confidence.  
 
The key to performing well lies in being genuine, maintaining a positive 
attitude, answering concisely yet clearly, and demonstrating awareness 
about one’s environment and chosen service. Candidates should avoid 
exaggeration, guesswork in factual questions, or defensive behavior 
when challenged. Good preparation involves thorough self -analysis, 
staying updated on national and international events, and practicing 
mock interviews to develop a calm, structured, and confident manner of 
communication.

Qualities—such as leadership, responsibility, adaptability, and

provides disaster relief. 
 Indian Navy: Protects maritime borders, ensures regional maritime stability, and 
conducts anti-piracy and humanitarian missions. 
 Indian Air Force: Ensures air superiority, conducts precision strikes, provides rapid

typically go through the following routes:

Academy). 
2. Indian Military Academy (IMA): After graduation, candidates can apply for 
IMA through the Combined Defence Services (CDS) exam, which includes written 
tests, SSB interviews, and medical exams. 
3. Indian Naval Academy (INA): Graduates can join the Indian Navy through the CDS 
or the direct entry scheme for specific technical branches. 
4. Air Force Academy (AFA): Graduates can apply for the Air Force through the 
CDS exam or other specialized routes for pilots and technical officers. 
5. Technical Entry Scheme (TES): For those with a technical background

while encouraging social responsibility and service to the community.

while enhancing personal growth and national contribution.

Also, the additional surprise challenges were kept to keep participants on their

Key Activities: 
 
 Marathon Run:  A marathon run is typiccaly conducted as a large,  
Organized road race in which participants cover a large distance . The event 
Began with an official start time, often using a staggered wave start system to  
Manage the large crowds. 
 
The volunteers are positioned throught o guide runners, ensure safety and   
Enforce Rules. Aid stations are placed at regular intervals – offering water, 
Energy gels and medical assistance. 
 
The race is concluded at designated finish line, where official times are recorded,  
Medals are awarded to finishers, and post-race recovery areas provide refreshments 
and first aid.

 Tug Of War :  
 Tug-of-war is a traditional team sport in which two opposing teams compete to 
pull a rope in opposite directions, with the goal of moving 
 a central marker or flag past a designated point on their side.  
 
 It is a test of strength, coordination, and teamwork, requiring participants to 
synchronize their efforts and maintain a steady rhythm to maximize pulling 
power.  
 
The game is usually played on a flat surface, such as grass, sand, or indoor 
flooring, with teams of equal numbers commonly eight members each,to ensure 
fairness.  
 
The contest begins on a referee’s signal, and teams must pull while keeping 
within their designated lanes, avoiding fouls such as sitting down, wrapping the 
rope around the body, or letting go.

 Tire Flip and Group Activity : 
The tire flip is a full-body, functional exercise often seen in strongman training 
and high-intensity workouts. 
 
 It begins with the athlete squatting low with a straight back, gripping the bottom 
of a large tire-typically a tractor or truck tire, and driving explosively through the 
legs, hips, and core to lift the tire from the ground using a “t riple extension” 
movement. 
 
As the tire rises, the lifter transitions their hands from an underhand to an 
overhand grip, stepping forward and using upper-body strength from the chest, 
arms, and shoulders to push the tire over. 
 
This compound motion engages nearly every major muscle group. 
Its explosive nature also improves functional fitness, coordination, mental 
toughness, and endurance, while doubling as an aerobic workout.  
 
However, proper technique is vital, as common mistakes —such as using the 
arms instead of legs for power, setting the hips too high, or applying uneven 
force—can increase risk of injury, especially to the back and biceps.

Conclusion: In conclusion, activitity  that demanded  physical endurance, 
strength, and skill also serve as powerful tools for developing both the body and 
mind. Cadets  built their  muscular power, cardiovascular health, and 
coordination while also enhancing discipline, resilience, and mental toughness. 
Beyond the measurable physical benefits, this  activity  fostered  teamwork, 
confidence, and a sense of achievement, encouraging individuals to push past 
limitations and discover new capabilities. Ultimately, Everyone  not only got  
test of physical ability but also opportunities for personal growth, community 
connection, and lifelong well-being.

Officers are the leaders and decision-makers in the military. To become one, candidates 
typically go through the following routes: 
1. National Defence Academy (NDA): After completing 12th grade, candidates can 
join the NDA, which offers a three-year training program, followed by training at 
respective service academies (Indian Military Academy, Naval Academy, or Air Force 
Academy). 
2. Indian Military Academy (IMA): After graduation, candidates can apply for 
IMA through the Combined Defence Services (CDS) exam, which includes written 
tests, SSB interviews, and medical exams. 
3. Indian Naval Academy (INA): Graduates can join the Indian Navy through the CDS 
or the direct entry scheme for specific technical branches. 
4. Air Force Academy (AFA): Graduates can apply for the Air Force through the 
CDS exam or other specialized routes for pilots and technical officers. 
5. Technical Entry Scheme (TES): For those with a technical background 
(engineering), this is a direct entry into officer ranks after class 12.

Key Activities: 
 
 Marathon Run:  A marathon run is typiccaly conducted as a large,  
Organized road race in which participants cover a large distance . The event 
Began with an official start time, often using a staggered wave start system to  
Manage the large crowds. 
 
The volunteers are positioned throught o guide runners, ensure safety and   
Enforce Rules. Aid stations are placed at regular intervals – offering water, 
Energy gels and medical assistance. 
 
The race is concluded at designated finish line, where official times are recorded,  
Medals are awarded to finishers, and post-race recovery areas provide refreshments 
and first aid.

--- Page 29 ---
 
 Tug Of War :  
 Tug-of-war is a traditional team sport in which two opposing teams compete to 
pull a rope in opposite directions, with the goal of moving 
 a central marker or flag past a designated point on their side.  
 
 It is a test of strength, coordination, and teamwork, requiring participants to 
synchronize their efforts and maintain a steady rhythm to maximize pulling 
power.  
 
The game is usually played on a flat surface, such as grass, sand, or indoor 
flooring, with teams of equal numbers commonly eight members each,to ensure 
fairness.  
 
The contest begins on a referee’s signal, and teams must pull while keeping 
within their designated lanes, avoiding fouls such as sitting down, wrapping the 
rope around the body, or letting go.  
 
  

--- Page 30 ---
 Tire Flip and Group Activity : 
The tire flip is a full-body, functional exercise often seen in strongman training 
and high-intensity workouts. 
 
 It begins with the athlete squatting low with a straight back, gripping the bottom 
of a large tire-typically a tractor or truck tire, and driving explosively through the 
legs, hips, and core to lift the tire from the ground using a “t riple extension” 
movement. 
 
As the tire rises, the lifter transitions their hands from an underhand to an 
overhand grip, stepping forward and using upper-body strength from the chest, 
arms, and shoulders to push the tire over. 
 
This compound motion engages nearly every major muscle group. 
Its explosive nature also improves functional fitness, coordination, mental 
toughness, and endurance, while doubling as an aerobic workout.  
 
However, proper technique is vital, as common mistakes —such as using the 
arms instead of legs for power, setting the hips too high, or applying uneven 
force—can increase risk of injury, especially to the back and biceps.

coordination while also enhancing discipline, resilience, and mental toughness.

confidence, and a sense of achievement, encouraging individuals to push past 
limitations and discover new capabilities. Ultimately, Everyone  not only got

Name of Club: National Service Scheme (NSS) 
Tagline: Not Me But You 
 
Establishment Year: - 24 September 1969 
 
Information about club: 
Establishing the National Service Scheme (NSS) was a visionary move by the Government of India 
in 1969, aimed at bridging the gap between students and the community. Inspired by the ideals of 
Mahatma Gandhi, the program's motto is "Not Me, But You." Here is a breakdown of the aims, 
objectives, and the diverse activities that define the NSS. 
 
1. Aims and Objectives 
The primary focus of NSS is the personality development of students through voluntary community 
service. It seeks to instil a sense of social responsibility and national integration. 
Core Objectives: 
 Social Consciousness: To understand the community in which they work and identify its 
needs and problems. 
 Problem Solving: To develop among themselves a sense of social and civic responsibility 
and find practical solutions to individual and community problems. 
 Leadership Skills: To acquire leadership qualities and a democratic attitude. 
 National Integration: To promote a sense of oneness and bridge the divide between different 
sections of society. 
 Skill Development: To develop the skills needed for mobilization of community 
participation. 
 
2. Regular Activities (Throughout the Year) 
Students (volunteers) are expected to complete 120 hours of service annually for two years. These 
activities usually happen on weekends or after college hours.

2 
 
 
Category 
 
Typical Activities 
 
 
Health & Hygiene 
 
Blood donation camps, immunization drives, and awareness about sanitation (Swachh Bharat 
Abhiyan). 
 
Environment 
 
Tree plantation (Van Mahotsav), plastic waste management, and water conservation projects. 
 
Education 
 
Adult literacy classes, tutoring underprivileged children, and digital literacy workshops. 
 
Social Issues 
 
Awareness campaigns against drug abuse, child marriage, and gender-based discrimination. 
 
Infrastructure 
 
Minor construction projects like levelling playgrounds or cleaning local ponds and monuments.

3 
 
 
3. Special Camping Program 
A major highlight of the NSS is the 7-day Special Camp, usually organized in a rural village or an 
urban slum. 
The Goal: Volunteers live among the community members, share their lifestyle, and work on a specific 
project that leaves a lasting impact on the locality. 
 Village Adoption: NSS units often "adopt" a village for 3–5 years to ensure sustained 
development. 
 Surveying: Conducting socio-economic surveys to help local government bodies understand the 
demographics. 
 Cultural Exchange: Evening programs where students and villagers perform together, fostering 
a deep cultural bond. 
 
4. National-Level Activities 
The NSS isn't just local; it offers opportunities for students to represent their institutions on a grander 
scale: 
 Republic Day Parade Camp: A prestigious camp in New Delhi where selected volunteers march 
on Kartavya Path. 
 National Integration Camps (NIC): Bringing volunteers from different states together to 
celebrate India's diversity. 
 Adventure Camps: Activities like trekking, paragliding, and basic mountaineering to build 
physical endurance and team spirit. 
 
Benefits for Students 
Beyond the altruistic satisfaction, being an NSS volunteer offers tangible rewards: 
1. NSS Certificate: Highly valued for higher education admissions and government job 
applications. 
2. Personality Growth: Improved communication, crisis management, and public speaking skills. 
3. Networking: Opportunities to meet people from diverse backgrounds and professional fields.

KIT Campus Cleanliness Program 
 
Date: Wednesday, 8 October 2025 
 
Time: 3:30 PM to 5:00 PM 
 
 
Introduction 
 
The National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of KIT College organized a campus - wide cleanliness  
drive on 8th October 2025. This initiative was undertaken in accordance with the Government of 
India’s cleanliness movement, which emphasizes the importance of maintaining hygiene, promoting 
sustainability, and creating plastic-free surroundings. 
The idea behind the program was to encourage students and staff to dedicate at least one hour to  
cleaning their surroundings on a regular basis. The campaign aligns with the broader vision

5 
 
of “Swachh Bharat Abhiyan” —a mission launched to achieve a cleaner, greener, and healthier 
nation. NSS volunteers actively participated in this progra m to contribute towards building a sense 
of civic responsibility and environmental awareness. 
Objective 
 
The “Campus Cleanliness” campaign was not just about cleaning the campus but also about 
cultivating a sense of ownership and discipline among students towards cleanliness. The main 
objectives were: 
1. To create awareness about the importance of cleanliness and hygiene among 
students and faculty. 
2. To promote a plastic -free environment by collecting and disposing of plastic 
waste in an eco-friendly manner. 
3. To instill a sense of responsibility and teamwork among NSS volunteers 
through active participation in social welfare activities. 
4. To support the Government of India’s mission of achieving a “Swachh Bharat” 
through community involvement. 
5. To inspire behavioral change among individuals, encouraging them to maintain 
cleanliness not only in college but also in their personal surroundings. 
Program Details 
 
The event began in the evening with a short inauguration session in the main college quadrangle. 
The NSS Program Officer addressed the volunteers and highlighted the significance  of the 
“Campus Cleanliness” campaign. The  volunteers were then  divided into several groups, each 
assigned specific areas within the campus, such as: 
 KIT Boys Hostel, KIT Girls Hostel 
 
 Main Building 
 
 Library, Gardens and parking areas 
 
 Mechanical , Civil Departments 
 
Each group was provided with gloves, masks, brooms, dustpans, and waste collection bags.

6 
 
The volunteers enthusiastically participated in cleaning their designated zones. They collected 
plastic bottles, wrappers, paper waste, and other non -biodegradable materials scattered across the 
premises. 
The collected waste was then sorted into biodegradable and non- biodegradable categories. 
Plastic waste was safely sent for disposal in accordance with eco-friendly practices. NSS volunteers 
also displayed banners and posters with slogans promoting cleanliness and discouraging plastic use. 
Conclusion 
 
The Campus Cleanliness Drive proved to be a meaningful and successful initiative conducted by the 
NSS unit of KIT College. The enthusiasm and dedication of the volunteers made the event not only 
impactful but also inspiring for others. 
The campaign emphasized that cleanliness is a collective duty and that every individual must 
contribute to keeping their surroundings clean and plastic-free. It also reminded everyone that small 
steps taken by individuals can lead to significant national change. 
The event concluded with a reaffirmation of the slogan: 
“स्वच्छता ही सेवा है, गंदगी जानलेवा ह ै। हर नागररक का हो ये सपना, स्वच्छ हो सम्प ूर्ण भारत अपना।” 
This message beautifully captured the essence of the day — that cleanliness is not merely a task but 
a service to the nation. The NSS volunteers pledged to continue this spi rit of service and maintain 
cleanliness as a lifelong practice.

Introduction 
 
The National Service Scheme (NSS) Unit of KIT's College of Engineering (Autonomous), 
Kolhapur organized a special program to bid farewell to senior NSS volunteers and warmly 
welcome the newly enrolled volunteers. The event aimed to recognize the valuable contributions of 
outgoing volunteers and inspire the new members to continue the legacy of service  with dedication 
and enthusiasm. The program reflected the true spirit of NSS, which focuses on community service, 
leadership development, and social responsibility. 
Objectives 
 
The main objective of the program was to appreciate and honor the senior volunteers for their sincere 
service and active participation in NSS activities throughout their journey. Another important goal 
was to introduce the newly enrolled volunteers to the vision, mission, and values  of NSS. The 
program also aimed to motivate the new members by sharing the real-life experiences and learnings 
of senior volunteers. In addition, it helped strengthen the bond  of teamwork, discipline, and unity 
among both senior and new NSS volunteers. 
Program Details 
 
The program was smoothly conducted and anchored by the existing NSS volunteers, who ensured 
proper coordination and active participation throughout  the event. The occasion was graced by  
Chief Guest Dr. Shivaji  Pawar,  
Medical Officer, Seva Bharti, Ichalkaranji, along with Registrar Dr.

students to actively participate in community service and contribute towards the betterment of 
society. 
During the ceremony, certificates were presented to the senior NSS volunteers in recognition of their 
dedication and active involvement in various social outreach programs such as blood donation

9 
 
camps, cleanliness drives, rural camps, and environmental awareness activities. Their continuous 
efforts and commitment to social service were appreciated by everyone present at the event. 
Additionally, trophies were awarded to a few outstanding volunteers who had shown exceptional  
dedication and leadership in NSS activities. These awards served as a recognition of their hard work 
and also as motivation for other volunteers. 
The senior volunteers also shared their memorable experiences and reflections from their NSS 
journey. They spoke about how NSS activities helped them develop leadership skills, teamwork, 
discipline, and a deeper understanding of social responsibility. They also expressed their gratitude to 
the faculty coordinators and the entire NSS team for their constant support and guidance. 
The newly enrolled NSS volunteers were warmly welcomed into the NSS family and encouraged to 
follow t he motto “Not Me, But You,” which represents the spirit of selfless service and 
commitment to society. 
Conclusion 
 
The Send-off and Welcome Function proved to be a meaningful and inspiring event  for all the 
volunteers present. It served as a platform to recognize the dedication of senior volunteers while 
motivating the new members to continue the mission of NSS with enthusiasm and responsibility. 
The program strengthened the sense of unity, teamwork, and commitment among the volunteers and

better and more responsible society.

Guest Lecture on Importance of Organ Donation DATE OF PROGRAM: 11 October 2025, 
Saturday 
TIME: 4:15 PM – 5:00 PM 
 
Introduction 
 
The National Service Scheme (NSS) Unit of KIT's College of Engineering (Autonomous), 
Kolhapur organized an  informative Guest Lecture on the “Importance of Organ Donation.” The 
purpose of this session was to educate students about the life-saving potential of organ donation and 
to create awareness about its social, ethical, and medical significance. The lecture  aimed to inspire 
students to develop a positive attitude toward organ donation and encourage them to spread 
awareness in society. 
Objectives 
 
The main objective of the lecture was to create awareness about the importance of organ donation 
and how it can help save multiple lives. The session also aimed to explain the medical, legal, and 
ethical aspects related to organ transplantation. Another goal was to motivate  students and NSS 
volunteers to develop a responsible and supportive attitude toward organ don ation. The lecture also 
encouraged students to actively participate in health awareness campaigns and social initiatives 
related to organ donation. 
Program Details 
 
The session was graced by Chief Guest Dr. Shivaji Pawar, Medical Officer, Seva Bharti, 
Ichalkaranji, who was warmly welcomed and introduced to the audience. Dr. Pawar was 
appreciated for his valuable contributions to community healthcare and social welfare. During  his 
lecture, he delivered an inspiring and informative talk on the importance of organ donation. He 
explained how a single organ donor can save the lives of several patients suffering  from serious 
medical conditions. Through real-life examples and experiences from his  medical practice, he 
helped students understand the emotional and social impact of organ donation on families and 
society.  
Dr. Pawar also explained important medical concepts related to organ donation such as brain death, 
cardiac death, living donors, deceased donors, organ compatibility, and donor registration

12 
 
systems. He highlighted the legal and ethical guidelines for organ donation in  India, helping 
students understand the process clearly. In addition, he discussed the future scope  of organ donation 
and emphasized the need to increase awareness in both urban and rural areas. He also mentioned the 
role of advanced medical technologies and improved healthcare systems in promoting successful 
organ transplantation. 
Interaction with Students 
 
The lecture concluded with an interactive question -and-answer session, where students actively 
participated and asked questions about eligibility for organ donation, registration procedures,  and 
common misconceptions  related to the topic. Dr. Pawar patiently  addressed each question and 
encouraged students to spread awareness about organ donation in their communities. 
Conclusion 
 
The guest lecture on “Importance of Organ Donation” by Dr. Shivaji Pawar proved to be a highly 
informative and inspiring session for all the students. His practical insights, real -life experiences, 
and motiv ational message encouraged students to  think positively about  organ donation and 
understand its importance in saving lives.

Details of Activities Conducted in A.Y. 2025-26 
 
Name of Club: National Service Scheme (NSS) 
Tagline: Not Me But You 
 
Establishment Year: - 24 September 1969 
 
Information about club: 
Establishing the National Service Scheme (NSS) was a visionary move by the Government of India 
in 1969, aimed at bridging the gap between students and the community. Inspired by the ideals of 
Mahatma Gandhi, the program's motto is "Not Me, But You." Here is a breakdown of the aims, 
objectives, and the diverse activities that define the NSS. 
 
1. Aims and Objectives 
The primary focus of NSS is the personality development of students through voluntary community 
service. It seeks to instil a sense of social responsibility and national integration. 
Core Objectives: 
 Social Consciousness: To understand the community in which they work and identify its 
needs and problems. 
 Problem Solving: To develop among themselves a sense of social and civic responsibility 
and find practical solutions to individual and community problems. 
 Leadership Skills: To acquire leadership qualities and a democratic attitude. 
 National Integration: To promote a sense of oneness and bridge the divide between different 
sections of society. 
 Skill Development: To develop the skills needed for mobilization of community 
participation. 
 
2. Regular Activities (Throughout the Year) 
Students (volunteers) are expected to complete 120 hours of service annually for two years. These 
activities usually happen on weekends or after college hours. 

--- Page 2 ---
 
2

Typical Activities 
 
 
Health & Hygiene 
 
Blood donation camps, immunization drives, and awareness about sanitation (Swachh Bharat 
Abhiyan). 
 
Environment 
 
Tree plantation (Van Mahotsav), plastic waste management, and water conservation projects. 
 
Education 
 
Adult literacy classes, tutoring underprivileged children, and digital literacy workshops. 
 
Social Issues 
 
Awareness campaigns against drug abuse, child marriage, and gender-based discrimination. 
 
Infrastructure 
 
Minor construction projects like levelling playgrounds or cleaning local ponds and monuments.

3 
 
 
3. Special Camping Program 
A major highlight of the NSS is the 7-day Special Camp, usually organized in a rural village or an 
urban slum. 
The Goal: Volunteers live among the community members, share their lifestyle, and work on a specific 
project that leaves a lasting impact on the locality. 
 Village Adoption: NSS units often "adopt" a village for 3–5 years to ensure sustained 
development. 
 Surveying: Conducting socio-economic surveys to help local government bodies understand the 
demographics. 
 Cultural Exchange: Evening programs where students and villagers perform together, fostering 
a deep cultural bond. 
 
4. National-Level Activities 
The NSS isn't just local; it offers opportunities for students to represent their institutions on a grander 
scale: 
 Republic Day Parade Camp: A prestigious camp in New Delhi where selected volunteers march 
on Kartavya Path. 
 National Integration Camps (NIC): Bringing volunteers from different states together to 
celebrate India's diversity. 
 Adventure Camps: Activities like trekking, paragliding, and basic mountaineering to build 
physical endurance and team spirit. 
 
Benefits for Students 
Beyond the altruistic satisfaction, being an NSS volunteer offers tangible rewards: 
1. NSS Certificate: Highly valued for higher education admissions and government job 
applications. 
2. Personality Growth: Improved communication, crisis management, and public speaking skills. 
3. Networking: Opportunities to meet people from diverse backgrounds and professional fields.

with disabilities and other students learn together in the same environment. The purpose of the visit 
was to understand the functioning of the school and to interact with the students through fun and 
educational activities. 
About the School 
 
Samarth Vidyamandir is located in Uchgaon near Kolhapur and is managed by the organization 
Helpers of the Handicapped. The main aim of the school is to provide equal education opportunities 
to both disabled and non -disabled students. The school provides a supportive learning environment 
and focuses on the overall development of students through academic learning,  sports, and cultural 
activities. It also has facilities such as laboratories, library, and 

--- Page 25 ---
 
25 
 
barrier- free infrastructure which helps students with disabilities move and learn comfortably. 
 
Activities Conducted During the Visit 
 
During our visit, the NSS volunteers organized several fun and interactive activities for the students. 
For the 6th standard students, we conducted activities such as Word Scramble and other small 
games. These activities helped students improve their think ing ability and vocabulary while 
enjoying learning process. The students participated with great enthusiasm and excitement. We also 
visited the pre-primary section where we interacted with small children. The volunteers spent time 
talking and playing with them. To make the moment special,  we distributed chocolates, which 
brought big smiles to their faces and created a joyful atmosphere. 
Experience and Learning 
 
The visit was a very enjoyable and memorable experience for all the volunteers. We observed that 
the school provides a positive and supportive environment for every child. The teachers and staff 
members are very dedicated and work hard for the development of students. Interacting with the 
children was the most heart-warming part of the visit. Their energy, innocence, and happiness made 
the experience very special. 
Conclusion 
 
The visit to Samarth Vidyamandir and Vidyalaya was both inspiring and informative. It helped 
us understand the importance of inclusive education and the role of educational inst itutions in 
supporting differently abled students. This experience motivated us to continue participating  in 
social service activities and to contribute towards building a more inclusive and caring society

Inclusive School, where children with and without disabilities study together, promoting confidence,

Road Safety Awareness Activity 
 
DATE : 29 April 2026 
 
Introduction: 
 
Road safety is a crucial aspect of daily life, ensuring the well -being of pedestrians, drivers, and 
commuters. With the rising number of road accidents, it has become essential to create awareness  
about traffic rules and safe commuting practices. To contribute to this cause, NSS volunteers 
organized a road safety awareness activity in Kolhapur city on 29th April 2026. This initiative 
aimed to educate the public about responsible road behavior and promote adherence to traffic 
regulations. 
 
 
 
Objective: 
 
The primary objective of this road safety awareness activity was to educate and sensitize the public 
regarding the importance of following traffic rules and ensuring road safety. Through interactive 
engagement, poster campaigns, and  discussions with traffic police, the initiative sought to 
encourage responsible road usage and reduce accident rates. 
 

--- Page 31 ---
 
31 
 
 
Event Structure and Flow: 
 
The activity began with the formation of volunteer groups, ensuring coverage across multiple 
locations in the city. Volunteers created posters with impactful road safety slogans to visually 
communicate key messages. These teams then proceeded to different areas, including Shivaji 
University, CIBER, Bindu Chowk, and Venus Corner, where they engaged directly with the public. 
Volunteers interacted with pedestrians, drivers, and commuters, emphasizing the importance of 
traffic regulations and responsible behavior on the road. Additionally, they collaborated with traffic 
police officers to understand their challenges in e nforcing road safety measures and reinforced the 
need for strict adherence to traffic rules. The volunteers actively  conveyed messages about wearing 
helmets, using seat belts, avoiding mobile phone usage while driving, and following traffic signals, 
thereby creating awareness through direct engagement. 
Impact: 
 
 Increased public awareness regarding road safety and responsible driving 
practices. 
 Strengthened collaboration between NSS volunteers and traffic authorities in 
promoting safe commuting. 
 Encouraged pedestrians and motorists to adopt safer road habits through direct 
engagement and information dissemination. 
 Helped reinforce the importance of following traffic rules to prevent accidents 
and ensure smooth traffic flow. 
Conclusion: 
 
The road safety awareness activity was a successful initiative led by NSS volunteers, making a 
significant impact on public awareness regarding traffic rules. Through active participation, creative 
posters, and meaningful discussions with traffic police and the public, this initiative contributed to 
the larger goal of reducing road accidents and fostering a culture of responsible commuting. Such  
efforts play a vital role in ensuring the safety of all road users and should be conducted regularly for 
long-term impact.

Report on Blood Donation Camp Date: 6th May 2026 
Centers: Central Library, Mechanical Department, MCA, VLSI Lab 
 
Associated Blood Banks: Mahatma Gandhi Hospital Blood Bank, Shahu Blood Bank and 
Sanjivani Blood Bank 
 
 
Introduction: 
 
On the proud occasion of Maharashtra Din and Kamgar Din, the NSS Unit organized a Blood 
Donation Camp on 6th May 2026 at four locations – the Central Library, the Mechanical  
Department, the MCA and VLSI Lab. The event aimed to inspire voluntary blood donation and 
contribute meaningfully to society. The camp received overwhelming participation from students, 
faculty, and staff, reflecting a strong spirit of service and compassion. 
Objective: 
 
The primary objective of the camp was to raise awareness about the importance of blood donation 
and to encourage students and faculty members to participate in this life-saving cause. The initiative 
also aimed to instill a sense of social responsibility among youth and provide an opportunity to 
contribute to public health by supporting local blood banks. 
Program Details: 
 
The camp was inaugurated with great enthusiasm.  The inauguration at the Central Library was 
done by Prof. Thoravat Sir , while the camp at the Mechanical Department was inaugurated by 
Dr. Jitendra Bhat Sir. The event saw a total of 131 pre-registrations through an online Google 
Form and 385 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
--- Page 34 ---
 
34 
 
spot entries on the day of the event, showcasing the enthusiasm and commitment of participants. 
The blood donation statistics from each center are as follows: 
 Central Library: 42 donors 
 
 Mechanical Department: 136 donors 
 
 VLSI Lab: 106 donors 
 
 MCA: 232 donors 
 
 Total Donations: 516 units of blood 
 
Each donor was acknowledged for their noble act by receiving a Earbuds and Speaker as a token of 
appreciation, which added a meaningful gesture to their contribution. 
To ensure smooth operations, NSS volunteers played an integral role at each center. Their 
responsibilities included: 
 Managing registrations (2 volunteers) 
 
 Coordinating center activities (2 volunteers) 
 
 Maintaining discipline 
 
 Serving refreshments post-donation 
 
The entire event was efficiently supervised by NSS Program Officer Dr. Nivas Patil ensuring 
professionalism and a supportive environment throughout the camp. 
Conclusion: 
 
The NSS Blood Donation Camp was a resounding success, both in terms of participation and 
impact. It served as a platform to promote humanitarian values and bring the academic community 
together for a noble cause. The generous contributions made by students and faculty will help save 
many lives and reinforce the message that “परार्थम् जीवितं यस्य स जीि व त” – One who lives for 
others, truly lives. The camp not only fulfilled its objective but also inspired many to continue 
contributing to society through such acts of kindness.

connected to the

The group discussed how Of ϐicer Like Qualities (OLQs) are not merely inborn traits but can 
be systematically developed through disciplined daily routines. Key points included 
maintaining physical ϐitness, time management, consistency, and a positive attitude. 
Participants emphasized that small daily habits like regular exercise, reading, leadership in 
group activities, and self-discipline gradually build qualities like responsibility, con ϐidence, 
and decision-making ability. Overall, the group agreed that consistent effort in daily life plays 
a crucial role in shaping an individual into an ofϐicer-like personality.

Date of Activity : (19/11/2025) 
Summary of Activity : 
Team LEAD INDIA organized an online quiz named “LEAD INDIA – Online Quiz” to assess 
students’ knowledge for UPSC preparation. The quiz was conducted through Google Form on 
14th November 2025 from 5:00 PM to 5:30 PM. A total of 25 questions were asked from 
subjects like Polity, History, Economy, Geography, Science, Current Affairs, and Logical 
Reasoning. The timed test helped improve time management, critical thinking, and quick 
recall of concepts. It also provided students with an opportunity for self-assessment and

Date of Activity : (15/01/2026) 
Summary of Activity : 
On 3 January 2026, the United States launched a large-scale military operation in Venezuela 
targeting the capital city Caracas. The operation resulted in the capture of Venezuelan 
President Nicola ́s Maduro and his transfer to the United States on criminal charges related 
to narco-terrorism and drug trafϐicking. Following this, the U.S. announced a transition plan 
involving new leadership and increased American inϐluence over Venezuela’s oil sector. 
Photographs –  
 
 
5) Name of the Activity : Interaction with Super Seniors 
 
Date of Activity : 29/01/2026 
Summary of Activity : 
Team Lead India conducted an online interaction session on 29 January 2026 through Google 
Meet with super senior Prathamesh Vidhate. The session focused on guidance for 
competitive exam preparation and doubt clearing. Students actively asked questions about 
study strategies, time management, and useful resources. Prathamesh shared his 
preparation methods, personal experiences, and practical tips, which motivated students and 
helped them improve their preparation approach and career planning. 
Photographs – Not any

Date of Activity : (31/01/2026) 
Summary of Activity : 
An interactive session was conducted on Saturday, 31 January 2026 through the Team LEAD 
India platform featuring Prof. Rajkumar Patil from Vidya Prabodhini, Kolhapur. The session 
aimed to create awareness among students about various administrative posts and

6 
 
competitive examinations. Students received basic guidance regarding career opportunities, 
preparation methods, and the importance of competitive exams. The session was interactive 
and informative, helping students gain valuable knowledge and motivation for future career 
planning. 
Photographs –   
 
6) Name of the Activity : Quiz Competition (Vidman) 
Date of Activity : (06/02/2026) 
Summary of Activity : 
VIDMAN Quiz Competition 2026 was a General Knowledge and CSAT-based competitive 
event organized to enhance students’ analytical thinking and awareness. The event received 
an overwhelming response, with nearly 1000 students registering and around 500 actively 
participating. It was conducted as an objective-type examination with 45–50 questions and 
included negative marking. The duration of the quiz was 45–60 minutes, and participation 
was completely free, ensuring accessibility for all students. 
Photographs –

7 
 
 
 
7) Name of the Activity : Debate on Democracy 
Date of Activity : (13/02/2026) 
Summary of Activity : 
Democracy is a system of government in which the people choose their leaders through 
elections. It supports freedom, equality, and participation of citizens in decision-making. It 
allows peaceful transfer of power and makes the government accountable to the public. 
 
However, democracy also has some drawbacks such as slow decision-making, corruption, 
inϐluence of money and power, and the possibility of uninformed voting due to illiteracy. 
 
In conclusion, democracy is considered the best form of government despite its limitations 
because it ensures people’s rights and freedom. Its success depends on responsible citizens 
and strong governance systems. 
 
Photographs –

8 
 
8) Name of the Activity : Discussion about our ancient sages 
Date of Activity : (26/02/2026) 
Summary of Activity : 
 A discussion was held on 27 February 2026 about the contributions and teachings of ancient 
Indian sages. The session highlighted how sages played an important role in shaping India’s 
cultural, spiritual, and intellectual heritage.  
Ancient sages such as Maharishi Veda Vyasa, Patanjali, Gautama Buddha, and others 
contributed greatly to philosophy, education, medicine, yoga, and literature. Their teachings 
focused on values like truth, discipline, self-control, non-violence, and harmony with nature. 
The discussion also emphasized how ancient texts like the Vedas, Upanishads, and epics such 
as the Mahabharata and Ramayana continue to guide moral and ethical living even today. 
In conclusion, the session helped students understand that the wisdom of ancient sages is 
still relevant in modern life and encourages us to follow a balanced and value-based lifestyle. 
Photographs –  
 
 
9) Name of the Activity : Conϐlict (wars) around the world and their impact on India 
Date of Activity : (06/03/2026) 
Summary of Activity : 
We mainly covered tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan, the United States, Israel, and 
Iran, China and Taiwan, and the Russia–Ukraine war. 
We also talked about civil wars happening in different countries and how they are causing 
instability and migration. 
After that, we discussed how these con ϐlicts affect India. We understood that the major 
impacts are rising fuel prices, increase in in ϐlation, disturbance in trade, and challenges in 
agriculture due to shortage of food and fertilizers. We also noted the safety concerns of 
Indians living abroad and the security challenges for our country.

9 
 
Finally, we concluded that even though these wars are not directly happening in India, they 
have a signiϐicant indirect impact. So, India needs strong foreign policy, energy security, and 
focus on self-reliance. 
Photographs –  
 
 
10) Name of the Activity : Extempore  
Date of Activity : (13/03/2026) 
Summary of Activity : 
The Extempore activity organized by the Lead India club was an engaging and thought-
provoking event aimed at enhancing students’ communication and critical thinking skills. 
Participants were given topics on the spot and were required to express their ideas 
conϐidently within a limited time. This activity helped students improve their spontaneity, 
clarity of thought, and public speaking abilities, which are essential for competitive exams 
and personal development. The event also created a positive learning environment where 
students could overcome stage fear and gain conϐidence. Overall, the extempore session was 
a successful initiative that encouraged active participation and contributed to the holistic 
development of students. 
 
Photographs –

10 
 
 
 
11) Name of the Activity : Interaction with Harshvardhan Pati 
Date of Activity : (18/03/2026) 
Summary of Activity : 
An interactive session was conducted through the Team LEAD India platform featuring 
Harshvardhan Patil (AIR 349, UPSC CSE 2025), a proud alumnus of KIT College. 
He completed his engineering in the Mechanical Department and was an active member of 
the Shourya Club. After graduation, he cleared the AFCAT (Air Force Common Admission 
Test); however, he could not continue further due to not qualifying in the medical 
examination. 
He then joined TCS (Tata Consultancy Services) and worked for nearly two years. During this 
period, he developed a strong interest in civil services. Later, he left his job and dedicated two 
full years exclusively to UPSC preparation. His consistent efforts led to success in his third 
attempt, where he secured All India Rank 349. 
Photographs –  
  
 
 
12) Name of the Activity : PPDT 
Date of Activity : (10/04/2026) 
Summary of Activity : 
A PPDT session was conducted on 10 April 2026 as part of personality and communication 
skill development activities. In this test, participants were shown a picture for a short 
duration and were asked to observe, perceive, and then narrate a meaningful story based on 
it.

11 
 
The activity aimed to evaluate observation skills, imagination, clarity of thought, and group 
discussion abilities. Each participant ϐirst wrote their individual story, and later a group 
discussion was held to arrive at a common storyline 
The session encouraged teamwork, con ϐidence in speaking, and the ability to listen and 
present ideas effectively. It also helped in improving quick thinking and structured 
communication under time pressure. 
In conclusion, the PPDT activity was useful in enhancing analytical thinking, communication 
skills, and overall personality development of the participants. 
Photographs –  
 
 
        
Dr. Priyanka N Mane 
Assistant Professor, 
Faculty Coordinator

1) Eco-Friendly Ganesh Idol Making Workshop Ganapati Festival – 
23/08/2025 
 
Program No.01: Eco-Friendly Ganesh Idol Making Workshop Ganapati Festival - 2025 
Event Name: Prarambha Introduction: 
The “Prarambha” event conducted during the Ganesh festival was a resounding success, aimed at 
creating awareness about the use of the eco-friendly Ganesh idols fostering a sense of responsibility 
towards environmental protection. This report outlines the key highlights and outcomes of the event. 
Event Objective: 
The primary objective of the “Prarambha” event was to raise awareness about the use of eco-friendly 
Ganesh idols made of natural soil or shadu instead of using the once made plaster of paris, which are 
harmful for the environment. By promoting eco-friendly practices, the event aimed to instill a sense 
of responsibility among participants towards protecting the environment and preserving natural 
resources. 
Additional objective we aimed at achieving was promoting the plantation of various indigenous 
varieties of plants. The eco-friendly Ganesh idol, crafted from natural soil, is infused with seeds 
from various plants. Once the festivities conclude, the idol can be safely transferred to a pot or 
garden, where it will sprout into a vibrant plant. This practice not only honors tradition but also 
nurtures the environment, symbolizing new beginnings (prarambha) and growth. 
Key Activities: 
Awareness Campaign: The event featured an awareness campaign highlighting the importance of 
eco-friendly Ganesh idols and the adverse effects of improper Visarjan of idols on the environment. 
Speaker Sessions: Speaker sessions were conducted to educate participants about simple and 
effective changes to traditional celebration of Ganesh festival which will be eco-friendly and 
contribute to the conservation of the environment. 
Demonstration: Demonstrations were organized to showcase the process of eco-Ganesh idol making 
by an expert professional simple and elegant methods. Participants were provided with materials and 
the know-how to create their own idols. participants learned about the importance of natural 
materials, the crafting process, and the benefits of choosing eco-friendly options. 
 
 
Hands-on Activity: This interactive session allowed everyone to create beautiful idols while also 
appreciating sustainability and traditional art, making it possible to celebrate the festival in an

3 
 
environmentally friendly way. 
 
 
Outcome: 
The "Prarambha " event succeeded in achieving its objectives by: 
- Creating awareness about eco-friendly Ganesh idols and eco-friendly celebration of festivals. 
- Educating participants about the importance of responsibilities towards the environment. 
- Encouraging participants to take proactive steps towards protecting the environment, by 
encouraging plantation trees. 
- Demonstrating that By making simple eco-friendly choices and encouraging others to do the 
same, we can make a big difference. This helps not only ourselves but also creates a healthier 
planet for future generations. 
Conclusion: 
The "Prarambha" event served as a platform for promoting eco-friendly practices and fostering a 
sense of environmental responsibility among participants. By advocating for the eco-friendly Ganesh 
idols, participants learned valuable lessons about sustainability and the importance of preserving the 
environment for future generations.

Report on Induction Program for F.Y. B.Tech Students -2025-26 
The First Year Student Induction Program was organized at Kolhapur Institute of Technology's, 
College Of Engineering Kolhapur (Empowered Autonomus) from 28, 29, 30 August 2025 (Part 
I) to 3 & 4 September 2025 (Part II)  with the primary goal of welcoming and orienting incoming 
new students with the academic environment, campus facilities, rules, rules, and culture of the 
institution. The major aim behind conducting the induction program was to ma ke the students 
aware of the academic culture, get acquainted with the new atmosphere and introduce the vision 
and missions of the institute.  The program consisted of a 5 -day’s orientation, with a diverse 
range of activities including academic sessions, ca mpus tours, student services presentations, 
workshops, and social events. 
Introduction 
As per the schedule given by AICTE for induction program, we the institute of Kolhapur 
Institute of Technology’s College of Engineering Kolhapur (Empowered Autonomous), 
scheduled all the activities and conducted successfully throughout different sessions such as 
morning, afternoon and evening every day, the Induction Program was held from 28, 29, 30 
August 2025 (Part I) to 3 & 4 September 2025 (Part II) . The time table fo r all the activities had 
prepared properly and according to the prepared time -table all the activities were conducted 
smoothly. Following is the list of all program cum activities conducted during induction 
program. 
1) Inauguration Function 
2) Information about Institute by Hon. Director. 
3) Learning Skills in carrier & technical education 
4) Beyond the Classroom: Discover Your Student Clubs. 
5) Statutory Mechanisms for Safeguarding Student Interests in Engineering Education 
6) Campus Compass: Finding Your Way with Mentors

18) Environmental Awareness 
19) Gender Equality 
20) Startup Eco-system 
 
The different sessions are briefly summarized below: 
1) Inauguration 
We started with a warm welcome from the faculty, all the Dean’s, HOD’s and staff. An official 
welcome speech given by Dean Student Activity Dr. Jitendra Bhat who highlighted the Institute's 
values and commitment to student success. Chief Guest Director Dr. Mohan Vanarotti briefed 
the information about Institute, encouraged and motivated students to be active and to involve  
sportively in all the activities at KITCoEK. Dr. Asif Qu reshi head of BSH briefed about First

Dr. Kulkarni briefed about statutory committee. She also highlighted the anti ragging

also be protected in a learning environment that promotes fairness, transparency, and growth. 
Engineering education is the foundation of technological advancemen t, and to build strong 
professionals, the system must be robust and student centric. Statutory mechanisms serve as 
the backbone to ensure this by providing legal and institutional frameworks that protect 
student rights and promote academic integrity. In co nclusion, statutory mechanisms are 
indispensable in safeguarding student interests in engineering education. They ensure not 
only the quality of education but also uphold the rights, dignity, and well -being of every 
student. As future engineers, understand ing and advocating for these protections helps us 
foster a culture of fairness, respect, and excellence.

surroundings. The speaker emphasized the alarming rise of pollution, deforestation, climate 
change, and the depletion of natural resources, stressing how human activities directly 
impact ecological balance. The session focused on simple yet effective step s that 
individuals can adopt, such as reducing plastic use, conserving water and energy, 
practicing waste segregation, and promoting afforestation. The importance of collective 
responsibility, sustainable lifestyle choices, and environmental education was strongly 
underlined. The main goal of environmental awareness was to foster a widespread 
understanding of the natural environment and the major issues affecting it.  The lecture by

Incubation Centre at KITCOEK, highlighting its mission to nurture innovative ideas  and 
support student-led startups. He inspired students to start looking for co-founders early, citing 
real-life success stories like Meesho, Ola, Elon Musk, and Mansukhbhai of Mitticool.

yourself, and stay curious.
